jobs.title: Compliance Specialist Air Quality
jobs.description:
Job Overview

APTIM is seeking an Environmental Scientist or Engineer with an air quality engineering background and 7–10 years of experience in air permitting and regulatory compliance. This position provides technical, permitting, and compliance support for a variety of emission sources, including landfill gas facilities.

The successful candidate will evaluate regulatory requirements, prepare permit applications and compliance reports, perform technical analyses, and develop practical solutions for clients. The role also supports business development through client relationship management and preparation of proposals, scopes of work, cost estimates, and technical approaches.

Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities

Prepare air permit applications and supporting documentation for major sources, Title V, Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD), synthetic minor, and minor sources, including permit modifications, renewals, and amendments.
Develop emission calculations and inventories for criteria pollutants, hazardous air pollutants, and greenhouse gases using client data, independent research, and applicable calculation methods.
Evaluate regulatory applicability, including New Source Performance Standards (NSPS), National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP), and New Source Review (NSR)/PSD requirements.
Interpret permit conditions and prepare compliance demonstrations, certifications, regulatory correspondence, and responses to agency inquiries.
Support environmental compliance for landfill gas facilities, including regulatory reporting, greenhouse gas reporting, Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA)-related obligations, and enforcement-related inquiries.
Provide continuity of permitting and compliance support during transitions in regulatory responsibilities.
Collect, interpret, and evaluate scientific and technical data using environmental databases, software, and emissions models to assess air quality and health risk impacts.
Perform technical and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) reviews of permit applications, emission inventories, compliance reports, technical memoranda, greenhouse gas submissions, and air dispersion modeling analyses.
Review stack testing protocols and reports and evaluate environmental monitoring, sampling, and testing programs.
Build and maintain client relationships, communicate technical findings, and recommend solutions to permitting and compliance challenges.
Evaluate proposed client projects to identify potential environmental impacts and permitting needs.
Support new business opportunities with existing and prospective clients by developing proposals, scopes of work, cost estimates, and technical approaches.
Support other environmental projects outside air quality as needed.

Basic Qualifications

Degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemical Engineering, Meteorology, or Physics.
7–10 years of relevant experience in air permitting and compliance, including minor source and Title V permitting.
Demonstrated knowledge of U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) air quality regulations, including NSPS and NESHAP.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical information clearly.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines.
Valid driver’s license and a driving record in good standing.

Desired/Preferred Qualifications

Experience performing mass flow, heat input, and emissions calculations.
Experience supporting municipal solid waste facilities, landfill gas collection systems, renewable natural gas (RNG) processes, flares, or similar environmental systems.
Experience with air permitting for generators.
Knowledge of Pennsylvania air quality regulations and Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (PADEP) permitting processes.
Experience using PADEP systems, including GreenPort, AESOnline, and RFDOnline.
Experience with New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC) Air Title V permitting and regulatory submissions.
Familiarity with CLCPA-related requirements, greenhouse gas reporting, and environmental compliance certifications.
Experience preparing Best Available Control Technology (BACT) analyses.
Experience preparing emission inventories and Title V reports using methods consistent with applicable state and local air district requirements.
Experience using AERMOD air dispersion modeling software.
Experience reviewing stack testing protocols, test reports, and environmental monitoring or sampling programs.
Demonstrated ability to conduct technical QA/QC reviews, identify regulatory risks, and communicate effectively with clients and regulatory agencies.
40-hour HAZWOPER certification.

About APTIM

APTIM enhances the quality of the environment, wellbeing of people, resilience of communities, and opportunity for employees to make a difference, not just a living. A leading professional solutions firm, we specialize in environmental, sustainability, resilience, and infrastructure solutions. Our team of experts provide these integrated solutions for forward-thinking government agencies, commercial and industrial clients, and energy customers. Together, we create sustainable and resilient communities for all.

What You Can Expect From APTIM

Work that is worthy of your time and talent
Respect and flexibility to live a full life at work and at home
Dogged determination to deliver for our clients and communities
A voice in making our company better
Investment into your personal and professional development

As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay range for this position is $87,000 to $99,000 per year. Compensation depends on several factors including: experience, education, key skills, geographic location of the position, client requirements, external market competitiveness, and internal equity among other employees within APTIM.

Employee Benefits

APTIM Environmental & Infrastructure, llc is committed to providing an extensive range of benefits that protect and promote the health and financial well-being of our employees and their families through the APTIM Benefits Marketplace https://aptim.makeityoursource.com/.

Medical, vision, and dental insurance: Through the marketplace, our employees can choose benefits from five metallic levels and several carriers to find the right benefits that work for them in their location.

jobs.title: Air Quality Environmental Analyst
jobs.description:
Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We have an opening for an Environmental Analyst
to support the Environment, Safety & Health (ESH) Directorate, Waste and Air Quality Office. You will provide advanced environmental regulatory compliance support in air quality to LLNL programs as well as support to the Environmental Functional Area (EFA) and ESH field Teams.

Depending on your assignment, this position may offer a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You may have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week.

This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level.

You will

Serve as a primary technical contact for the EPA, California Air Resources Board (CARB), and local Air Districts.
Interpret complex air compliance regulations and legislation, negotiate the best compliance solution with regulators, prepare detailed air permit applications and permit related documents, and serve as a resource for and/or collaborate with LLNL stakeholders.
Analyze, interpret, and provide guidance on proposed federal, state, and local complex environmental regulations and DOE Orders as they may relate to LLNL operations.
Conduct complex environmental analyses and audits of operations and facilities to identify potential environmental issues and recommend solutions.
Coordinate and participate in regulatory inspections, audits, and site verifications by internal and external agencies.
Perform data analysis including statistical analysis of environmental data; maintain spreadsheets.
Review air dispersion modeling and human health risk assessment modeling analyses as needed.
Work independently and in a team environment with minimal direction depending on assigned tasks.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Additional Job Responsibilities, At The TSS.4 Level

Serve as a primary technical contact for environmental air regulatory compliance and interpret highly complex environmental regulations and legislation, negotiate the best compliance solution with regulators, prepare detailed applications and permit related documents and serve as a resource and/or collaborate with LLNL programs.
Analyze proposed federal, state, and local highly complex environmental regulations and DOE requirements on orders for legal and potential impacts to LLNL operations.
Conduct highly complex environmental analyses and audits of operations and facilities to identify potential environmental issues and recommend solutions.
Mentor and train junior staff in technical skills, knowledge, and abilities.

Qualifications

Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship.
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Physical, Chemical, Biological, Atmospheric, or Environmental Sciences, Engineering or related field, or equivalent combination of education and related experience.
Significant knowledge and experience in federal, state, and local air regulations.
Experience analyzing, interpreting, and assessing compliance of complex environmental regulations and recommending solutions.
Advanced experience conducting audits and compliance inspections.
Advanced verbal and written communication skills necessary to effectively present, explain and communicate complex technical information to all levels of personnel and management; ability to handle sensitive and confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment.
Analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving skills to evaluate, interpret, negotiate, recommend, and implement actions/solutions for complex problems which may involve data and modeling analysis.
Effective organizational skills with detail orientation necessary to handle multiple complex tasks in a demanding environment with conflicting priorities, tight and changing deadlines, and frequent interruptions while providing high-level customer service, and good follow-through.

Additional Qualifications At The TSS.4 Level

Highly advanced knowledge and substantial experience in air compliance programs.
Highly advanced experience analyzing, interpreting, and assessing compliance with highly complex environmental regulations and recommending and implementing solutions.
Experience mentoring and training junior staff on relevant skills, knowledge, and abilities.

Qualifications We Desire

Master’s degree in engineering, environmental science, or related field.
Experience with Bay Area Air Quality Management and/or San Joaquin Valley Air Pollution Control District regulations.
Experience with the management of air quality instrumentation/networks including installation, maintenance, and trouble shooting.
Knowledge and experience with other relating environmental regulatory and compliance requirements, including NEPA, CEQA, hazardous waste, stormwater, drinking water at the state and federal levels.

Pay Range: $154,950 - $235,692 Annually

$154,950 - $196,476 Annually for the TSS.3 level

$185,850 - $235,692 Annually for the TSS.4 level

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting; pay will not be below any applicable local minimum wage. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, speciﬁc competencies, relevant education, qualiﬁcations, certiﬁcations, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Additional Information

Position Information

This is a Flexible Term appointment, which is for a definite period not to exceed six years. If final candidate is a Career Indefinite employee, Career Indefinite status may be maintained (should funding allow).

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
Flexible Benefits Package
401(k)
Relocation Assistance
Education Reimbursement Program
Flexible schedules (*depending on project needs)
Our values - visit https://www.llnl.gov/inclusion/our-values

Security Clearance

This position requires a Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance. If you are selected, we will initiate a Federal background investigation to determine if you meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information or matter. Also, all L or Q cleared employees are subject to random drug testing. Q-level clearance requires U.S. citizenship.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

How To Identify Fake Job Advertisements

Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. LLNL never extends an offer without a personal interview and will never charge a fee for joining our company. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

To learn more about recruitment scams: https://www.llnl.gov/sites/www/files/2023-05/LLNL-Job-Fraud-Statement-Updated-4.26.23.pdf

Equal Employment Opportunity

We are an equal opportunity employer that is committed to providing all with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, protected veteran status, age, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Reasonable Accommodation

Our goal is to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates applying and interviewing at the Laboratory. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please use our online form to submit a request.

California Privacy Notice

The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) grants privacy rights to all California residents. The law also entitles job applicants, employees, and non-employee workers to be notified of what personal information LLNL collects and for what purpose. The Employee Privacy Notice can be accessed here.

Dare to learn new skills, advance in your career and make an impact at Henkel
.

This role will also serve as a liaison for regulatory affairs with outside parties, such as regulatory organizations, stakeholders and external consultants.

This role sits at the intersection of toxicology, regulatory science, consumer safety and product development.

PhD or Master in field of Toxicology

Why Black & Veatch?

At Black & Veatch, you’ll be part of work that matters—designing, creating, and building the infrastructure communities rely on every day, from concept through execution.

We care about how the work gets done as much as what we build. Safety is built into every decision, and people look out for each other—speaking up, collaborating, and doing the right thing because it affects real lives.

You’ll work alongside teams solving complex challenges and turning ideas into solutions that perform in the real world—gaining hands-on experience across projects, technologies, and disciplines.

Ownership shows up in how we work. We take responsibility for outcomes, follow through on commitments, and take pride in what we deliver. As a 100% employee-owned company, employees share in the long-term success we build together.

With flexible ways of working and meaningful development opportunities, you’ll build a career you can be proud to stand behind.

The Opportunity

In this role as a Staff Environmental Sciences Specialist
, you will have the opportunity to: 

Work with a dynamic team within an established global infrastructure consulting and engineering company. 
Work as part of a team of environmental scientists and consultants to support our clients in achieving compliance with a wide range of state and federal environmental programs and regulations spanning multiple environmental media through every phase of a project; from feasibility, to design, to construction, to operations.  
Join Black & Veatch’s Environmental practice to work with a team of professionals focused on ensuring environmental stewardship for our clients. 

The Team

Our Environmental team is a multidisciplinary team of ecologists, engineers, scientists, project managers, and attorneys working together to identify optimum environmental solutions for our clients.  We have provided environmental consulting services in support of projects for over 40 years including a diverse and growing mix of infrastructure projects such as power generation (conventional and renewable) and transmission, oil and gas facilities and pipelines, water and wastewater treatment facilities, data centers, and food and beverage industries. As a full-service environmental consulting practice, services include impact assessment and planning, regulatory compliance and permitting, wetland and floodplain analysis, waterbody and water quality assessment, air quality permitting and management, environmental remediation, site due diligence, environmental noise assessment, pollution prevention planning, and climate action solutions.

Environmental | Black & Veatch

Key Responsibilities

Lead and support National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permitting and compliance projects for municipal and industrial wastewater treatment facilities and industrial dischargers across the United States.
Prepare new, renewal, and modification applications for individual and general NPDES permits, including technical narratives, process descriptions, wastewater characterization evaluations, flow and pollutant loading evaluations, treatment system assessments, sampling and monitoring plans, antidegradation demonstrations, and supporting documentation.
Evaluate regulatory applicability, permitting and compliance strategies under the Clean Water Act, federal and state NPDES programs, and local pretreatment programs, including requirements for direct discharges, indirect discharges, pretreatment, and land application or reuse where applicable.
Review and interpret technology-based and water quality-based effluent limitations, water quality standards, total maximum daily loads, mixing -zone requirements, reasonable potential analyses, and antidegradation requirements, and Clean Water Act Sections 316(a) and 316(b) requirements, including thermal discharge demonstrations and cooling water intake structure evaluations.
Assess wastewater characterization data, discharge monitoring reports, compliance histories, treatment performance, and proposed facility changes to identify permitting risks and practical compliance solutions.
Coordinate with facility owners, operators, engineers, laboratories, legal counsel, and federal, state, and local permitting authorities throughout permit development, agency review, negotiation, public notice, and final permit issuance.
Support and lead the development and implementation of permit compliance programs, including monitoring and reporting plans, operational stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPPs) discharge monitoring data evaluations, best management practices, compliance schedules, corrective action plans and responses to agency information requests, notices of violation, or enforcement matters.
Provide technical guidance to multidisciplinary project teams on wastewater permitting considerations during planning, design, construction, startup, and operation of treatment systems and related infrastructure.
Manage assigned scopes, schedules, budgets, deliverables, and client communications; contribute to proposals and business development for wastewater permitting and compliance services.
Conduct occasional site visits and field reviews to understand wastewater generation, treatment processes, discharge locations, and compliance conditions.

Management Responsibilities

Individual Contributor

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental engineering, civil engineering, chemical engineering, environmental science, or a related field; advanced degree in a relevant discipline is a plus.
Five to ten years of progressive experience in industrial and/or municipal wastewater permitting, regulatory compliance, or environmental consulting, with substantial experience preparing or supporting NPDES permit applications in the United States.
Demonstrated experience with industrial and/or municipal wastewater treatment facilities, including familiarity with treatment processes, wastewater characterization, monitoring programs, operational considerations, and regulatory requirements that affect permit conditions. Experience supporting Clean Water Act Section 316(a) and Section 316(b) studies, evaluations, or compliance programs is highly desirable.
Experience and knowledge of wastewater and related utility systems that support data centers, power plants, municipal wastewater treatment facilities, manufacturing operations, pharmaceutical facilities, mining and other industrial operations is a plus.
Working knowledge of the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Parts 122–125, applicable effluent limitation guidelines, antidegradation requirements, state water quality standards, and delegated state NPDES permitting programs.
Experience evaluating and developing technology-based and water quality-based effluent limitations, including analyses of receiving-water characteristics, water quality data, reasonable potential, antidegradation requirements, total maximum daily loads, mixing zones, compliance schedules, and other permit development considerations.
Experience with industrial pretreatment requirements, categorical pretreatment standards, indirect wastewater discharge permitting, or municipal pretreatment programs, including local limits development is highly desirable.
Experience communicating and negotiating with EPA, state environmental agencies, publicly owned treatment works, and other permitting authorities.
Ability to analyze technical and regulatory information, identify permitting risks, and develop practical, defensible strategies for clients and project teams.
Strong technical writing, verbal communication, project coordination, and client-service skills, with the ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines.
Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer in Training (EIT) certification is preferred for engineering-degree candidates Certified Environmental Professional (CEP), or Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM), as applicable to the candidate’s background and responsibilities.
Completion of recognized NPDES, wastewater compliance, pretreatment, or water quality training is a plus.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, environmental science, or a related scientific discipline, or relevant specialized training and experience that uniquely qualify the individual to perform the job responsibilities.
Minimum of 5 years of related professional experience in environmental permitting or compliance, including direct experience with NPDES wastewater discharge permitting and the national pretreatment program. Candidates with approximately 5–10 years of relevant experience are preferred for this role.
Experience preparing technical documents, permit applications, or compliance deliverables for industrial or municipal wastewater treatment facilities in the United States.
Ability to travel domestically for client meetings, agency meetings, and occasional site visits.
All applicants must be able to complete pre-employment onboarding requirements (if selected), which may include any or all of the following: criminal/civil background check, drug screen, and motor vehicle records search, in compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

Work Environment/Physical Demands

Hybrid or flexible work options may be offered after the first 90 days of employment based upon manager discretion, job performance and work assignments.
Ability to utilize audio/videoconferencing software tools for internal/external communication
Sitting/standing/computer usage for extended periods of time
Domestic travel is required

Compensation Transparency

In accordance with local requirements, the annual compensation ranges for this role are listed below by state or jurisdiction and reflect the applicable office location(s) within each. jobs.description:
Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company which provides a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries. The Group believes it is the world leader in food, environment and pharmaceutical products testing and in agroscience CRO services. It is also one of the global independent market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and for supporting clinical studies. In addition, Eurofins is one of the key emerging players in specialty clinical diagnostic testing in Europe and the USA.

Group's key figures are approx. 6.95 billion Euros turnover, over 950 laboratories across 60 countries and about 63,000 staff.

Job Description

Eurofins Environment Testing in Parsippany NJ is looking for a full-time Service Center Supervisor. The hours are Monday-Friday 8am-5pm plus overtime as needed. Compensation is $23-26/hour (Depends on Experience). Must live a commutable distance to Parsippany NJ.

The Service Center Supervisor (SCS) manages the service center and acts as a liaison between the laboratory and the local client base. The SCS is in charge of supervising the Service Center facility, supervising service center couriers, samplers and other personnel. The SCS will consistently act in the best interest of Eurofins Environment Testing America and exhibit professional behavior and performance with both internal and external clients. Eurofins Environment Testing America and the SCS are committed to grow the business through a Client-First culture that will provide exemplary client service.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Local area primary client representative for service center location.
Works with the Quality Assurance Manager and Account Executives to evaluate and establish project requirements for the service center area.
Ensures client complaints are handled professionally and resolved in a timely manner.
Maintain records for the vehicle maintenance and driving miles; reporting it in at the end of each month.
Supervising service center couriers, scheduling pickups and deliveries, preparing bottle orders, and shipping samples to the designated laboratory for analysis.
Works closely with laboratory management in laboratory capacity loading decisions.
Maintains the facilities at the service center and is responsible for all EH&S policies of Eurofins Environment Testing at the service center.
Provides general sales support to Account Executives for business development activities started in the field.
Orders supplies (bottles, coolers, etc.) for the service center
Maintains knowledge of method requirements, holding times, and bottle requirements in order to assist clients with their project needs.
Maintains knowledge of all Eurofins Environment Testing laboratories to assist with placement of projects into the appropriate laboratory to best fit the clients’ needs.
Builds local relationships with clients and regulatory agencies.
Visits clients on own or with local sales staff.
Provides courier services as needed to support local client needs
Supervises a geographically dispersed team
Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Basic Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma Required
Field Services experience preferred
Prior supervisory experience required

Experience working directly with customers, serving as a trusted point of contact, resolving concerns, and representing the company in a professional manner.
A valid state issued driver’s license to drive company vehicles is required as an employee with driving responsibilities. Clean driving record to drive company vehicle.

Ability to lift up to 50 pounds. Samples will be in coolers packed in ice.
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English.
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship

Preferred Ability and Skills:

Professional, knowledgeable, confident, and friendly demeanor
Customer service experience
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Must be detail oriented with the ability to speak, read, and write English fluently
Must have the ability to follow complex instructions
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail and a willingness to meet daily commitments with a widely varying workload
Ability to handle multiple details and changing priorities
Ability to read maps and follow directions
Ability to operate a motor vehicle
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, self-motivation, adaptability, and a positive attitude

Additional Information

Please note - Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. This role provides leadership, technical expertise, and strategic direction to management and employees on environmental, health, ergonomic, safety, and security initiatives. The EHS&S Manager partners with facility leadership to identify and address risks, implement preventative measures, ensure compliance with applicable regulations, and drive a culture of safety throughout the organization.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Lead and manage the facility’s environmental, health, safety, and security (EHS&S) programs and continuous improvement initiatives.
Develop, implement, and maintain EHS&S policies, procedures, and written programs including Lockout/Tagout, Confined Space Entry, Mobile Equipment Safety, Fall Protection, Electrical Safety, Hearing Conservation, Hazard Communication, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), Emergency Action Plans, Security Programs, Bloodborne Pathogens, Waste Management, Spill Response, and Storm Water Management.
Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, DOT, state, local, and company safety and environmental requirements.
Serve as the primary facility resource and contact for regulatory agencies and compliance-related matters.
Prepare, maintain, and submit all required environmental reports and documentation accurately and on time.
Manage the development and administration of Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs) and associated document control processes.
Lead the facility safety committee and partner with plant leadership to achieve company and site-specific safety objectives.
Conduct safety inspections, audits, and risk assessments to identify opportunities for improvement.
Develop and facilitate EHS&S training programs for employees and leadership teams.
Measure, analyze, and communicate key safety and environmental performance metrics.
Build and maintain accountability systems that reinforce safety ownership at all levels of the organization.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate EHS&S priorities into daily operations and business objectives.
Support Human Resources with new hire safety orientation and return-to-work programs.
Evaluate workplace hazards and implement effective controls to mitigate risk.
Conduct incident investigations and root cause analyses to identify corrective and preventive actions.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Strong knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental, health, and safety regulations and industry standards.
Working knowledge of manufacturing operations, processes, and safety practices.

Strong interpersonal skills and ability to influence positive change across all levels of the organization.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, spreadsheets, databases, and presentation software.
Ability to read, write, speak, and comprehend English.
Emergency response, First Aid, and CPR training experience preferred.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field; or
Seven (7) years of related EHS experience and/or training; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience supporting safety programs within a manufacturing environment strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to maintain current knowledge of applicable federal, state, local, and company safety and environmental regulations.

Required to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) and comply with all company safety policies and procedures.
Ability to work in both office and manufacturing environments.
Ability to move throughout production, warehouse, and job site environments.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, bend, stoop, twist, and climb as needed.

At the University of Canberra, we’re a welcoming and connected academic community shaped by the people, cultures and environments of Australia’s capital. Our research focuses on real-world challenges, working alongside partners to create outcomes that matter, while our teaching builds confidence and capability for the future. The Faculty of Science & Health
is a dynamic and research-intensive academic community dedicated to improving health, wellbeing and quality of life through excellence in teaching, research, innovation and engagement.
Bringing together expertise across nursing, midwifery, rehabilitation, sport and exercise science, behavioural and human sciences, public health, psychology, social work, disability, biomedical science, environmental science and applied health sciences, the Faculty fosters a highly collaborative and interdisciplinary environment where researchers, educators and industry partners work together to address some of society's most pressing health, environmental and social challenges.

About the role:

We are seeking an enthusiastic and collaborative academic to join our Environmental Science team as a Lecturer in Environmental Science. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a growing and research-active discipline while helping to educate the next generation of environmental professionals.
As a Lecturer, you will play a key role in delivering outstanding teaching, building a successful research profile, supervising student research projects, and engaging with industry, government and community partners. Your work will contribute to the University's commitment to addressing contemporary environmental challenges and strengthening our research impact.
Please note:
For this role, we are open to consider suitable candidates at either Lecturer (Academic Level B) or Senior Lecturer level (Academic Level C).

Key responsibilities:

Teach and coordinate undergraduate and postgraduate units in Environmental Science and related disciplines.
Deliver engaging and inclusive learning experiences across face-to-face, blended and online settings.
Design, review and enhance curriculum, assessment and learning resources to support student success and graduate employability.
Develop and grow a research program aligned with the University's environmental research strengths.
Publish high-quality research outputs and seek competitive research funding.
Supervise undergraduate research projects, Honours students and HDR candidates.
Maintain high standards of research integrity, ethics, safety and professional practice.

About you:

To be successful in this role, you will bring:
A completed doctoral qualification in Applied Environmental Science or a closely related discipline.
Demonstrated ability to teach and convene relevant units effectively across face-to-face, blended and online modes.
Demonstrated capacity to supervise undergraduate projects, Honours students, and HDR candidates effectively.
Expertise in an area aligned with the current research strengths in Applied Environmental Science: freshwater ecology, ecosystem processes, conservation ecology, genomics, or related fields
A developing or established track record of high-quality research publications.
Excellent communication, organisational and interpersonal skills.
A commitment to inclusion, diversity, cultural safety and student-centred learning.

Seton Hall University invites applications for a full-time tenure-track professor at the rank of Assistant Professor in the Department of Biological Sciences to start Fall 2027, pending final budgetary approval.

The Department of Biological Sciences is undergoing rapid growth and seeks to develop coursework and research in environmental sciences and related fields.

The Department of Biological Sciences offers a diverse research environment including PhD/MS graduate programs, core facilities, and a collaborative environment. Additional information on the department and its research faculty is described here: https://www.shu.edu/biology/index.cfm

Seton Hall University is located in South Orange, New Jersey, 14 miles from New York City. It is the oldest Catholic diocesan institution of higher education in the United States and is home to about 6,300 undergraduate and 4,700 graduate students. A vibrant and culturally diverse community, Seton Hall pursues academic excellence and ethical development in a collaborative environment and prepares its students to be servant leaders in their professional and community lives. Seton Hall University is an Equal Opportunity employer. It honors diverse perspectives and respects the religious commitments of all its employees. In turn, its faculty respect Catholic beliefs and values, engage the Catholic Intellectual Tradition, and support the University's mission as a Catholic institution of higher education.

Duties And Responsibilities

The successful candidate will develop a research program that involves both undergraduate and graduate students and can be externally funded. The position includes teaching biology major required courses, ecology focused courses, as well as graduate courses within their area of expertise. Faculty are also expected to mentor Graduate students' research; offer experiential research opportunities with advising to undergraduate students; and provide services to the department, college, and university.

More specifically, the hire would be expected to (1) run a core biology courses & support the biology majors in all sciences; (2) increase the variety of upper-level bio-electives by offering new courses such as Sustainable Agriculture and Habitat Restoration or Environmental Toxicology and participate in the ongoing creation of academic programs in Environmental Science; (3) assist with educating, managing, mentoring, and advising the increased number of biology majors; (4) provide a computational-based research space for undergrads and graduate students; (5) assist with all the day today activities that are important to a functional department; and (6), just as importantly, the faculty member will participate in innovative, collaborative program development in interdisciplinary STEM fields as part of our "STEM Initiative." This concentration will provide student support for occupations in "Green Fields" including environmental engineering, conservation scientists, and urban planning.

Required Qualifications

Applicants must have a Ph.D. or equivalent degree in Environmental Sciences or related fields (Ecology, Marine Biology, Environmental Science, Plant Biology, Botany, Geology, Earth Science). Preferred candidates would have 2yrs of relevant postdoctoral training, a strong publication record, and previous teaching experience at the college level. (ABDs will be considered)

Desired Qualifications

Applicants will be expected to establish and sustain an energetic, externally funded research program. The successful candidate will mentor graduate student research/projects and offer experiential research opportunities to undergraduate students.

The candidate will teach graduate and undergraduate students. Courses will include general biology major courses, upper-level biology major electives, as well as graduate courses in his/her area of expertise.

The University is interested in expanding its programming in environmental sciences and engineering, and the ideal candidate would be interested in contributing to that effort.

They will engage in service for the department, college, and university, including, but not limited to, committee work and undergraduate student advising.

Cover letter including job code number

Curriculum vitae

3-page research plan

Teaching philosophy

3 current letters of references

Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Applications received before December 1, 2026 will receive priority review

jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

Job Description

Position Summary:

The Associate Chemist prepares and analyzes environmental samples using standard analytical techniques according to approved scientific methodology in compliance with Eurofins Environment Testing Quality Assurance programs and standard operating procedures (SOPs). This position can be a physical job that may require standing for long periods, working with organic solvents, laboratory glassware and specialized equipment.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Performs routine lab tasks that provide experience and familiarization with methods, practices, and programs. These include:
Preparation of samples using standard techniques
Performing chemical analysis using standard techniques
Evaluation and quantification of data
Recording and reporting data and any unusual test occurrences to the supervisor
Performing routine instrument maintenance

Competency in complex instrumentation instrument specific software (training is provided)
Responsible for keeping personal training documentation (training records, IDOC/DOC) current and accurate
Responsible for timely completion of assigned/scheduled QC samples (MDL, LOD/LOQ, PT)
As required, documents NCMs for projects with quality issues
Understands and utilizes backlog reports to manage personal workload
Works under close supervision using routine and standard methods
Regular attendance and punctuality
Responsible for general housekeeping in work area
Proficient with IDOCs, for assigned methods carried out in the department
Responsible for performing job functions in compliance with Eurofins Environment health and safety and quality assurance standards
Demonstrates and promotes the company vision
Inventories and stocks laboratory supplies
Washes and inventories glassware
Purges analyzed samples
Assists in other areas of laboratory when needed
Additional duties as assigned

Follow and learn appropriate protocols in one or more of the following disciplines. This role will focus on PFAS Analysis and LC/MS.

Organic preparation
Metals preparation and analysis
PFAS sample preparation
HRMS sample preparation
Gas Chromatography
Liquid Chromatography
Mass Spectrometry
Radio Chemistry
Wet Chemistry
High Resolution preparation and analysis
Low Resolution preparation and analysis

This position is 2nd shift, Sun-Thurs, 3pm -1130pm. Training will be M-F 7am-3:30pm.

Qualifications

Basic Minimum Qualifications

BS or BA in Chemistry or related field, Associate Degree, or 2 years of related laboratory experience in lieu of degree.
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English.
Authorization to work in the United States without restriction or sponsorship

Ideal Candidates Will Have

Previous experience with PFAS and/or LC/MS
Previous experience in a lab or production setting
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
Able to interpret written materials and communicate findings effectively.
Demonstrated ability to identify issues, analyze root causes, and propose practical solutions.
Applies critical thinking to evaluate options and make decisions.
Effective collaboration skills to contribute to team goals and support department productivity goals
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage priorities and meet deadlines.
Effectively balances multiple tasks while maintaining accuracy.
Comfortable using mathematical formulas and tools to perform calculations and analyze data.
Consistently delivers high-quality work within established timelines and specifications.
Able to work independently, following written or verbal instructions with minimal oversight.
Strong interpersonal skills; able to coordinate tasks and communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.

Additional Information

Pay rate: $18-19/hour + 10% shift differential

Please note - Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

The benefits package offered will vary based on the employee’s full-time or part-time regular status.

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and Eurofins Scientific agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialized and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralized and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

jobs.description:
RahrBSG is looking for a Environmental Compliance Manager in Shakopee, Minnesota. The Environmental Compliance Manager leads environmental compliance and sustainability programs across Rahr Corporation and its subsidiaries, ensuring adherence to federal, state, provincial, and local environmental regulations. As the organization's environmental subject matter expert, this role provides strategic oversight for permitting, compliance assurance, environmental risk management, and environmental management systems, with a strong focus on air quality, water, wastewater, stormwater, waste, and chemical management programs. Partnering closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, and business leaders, the Environmental Compliance Manager supports operational excellence, protects the company's ability to operate, and advances long-term business growth through proactive environmental stewardship and risk reduction.

BENEFITS & PERKS:

Competitive Starting Base Salary between $120,000 - $140,000 annually 

Annual Bonus

Medical benefits with coverage paid for at 90%

Dental and Vision Programs

Generous Annual 401(k) Company Contribution of 15%

Employee Assistance Program

Paid Life Insurance

Short Term Disability

Long Term Disability

Tuition Reimbursement

Generous PTO

Sick Time

12 Paid Company Holidays

Parental Leave

Career Growth and Progression Paths

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Environmental Compliance Leadership

Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of corporate environmental compliance programs.

Monitor and interpret environmental regulations and communicate compliance obligations to business leaders.

Ensure facilities maintain compliance with all applicable environmental permits, licenses, registrations, plans, and approvals.

Provide strategic guidance and technical expertise to site leadership regarding environmental risks, regulatory requirements, permitting obligations, and compliance strategies.

Develop environmental standards, procedures, and best practices applicable across all operating companies.

Manage 3rd Party Consultants and Attorneys

Provide options for compliance paths to management

Review permits, amendments and cap-ex additions for compliance and defensibility

Remain current on environmental regulatory initiatives, enforcement trends, emphasis programs, and emerging issues to proactively assess impacts on business operations and compliance obligations

Permitting and Regulatory Management

Lead environmental permitting strategies for new capital projects, facility expansions, and operational changes.

Oversee environmental permit applications, modifications, renewals, registrations, and compliance certifications.

Serve as corporate lead for air permitting, wastewater permitting, stormwater permitting, and waste-related regulatory obligations.

Interface directly with regulatory agencies, consultants, attorneys, and external stakeholders.

Support agency inspections, audits, information requests, and enforcement actions as required.

Coordinate environmental compliance reporting and regulatory submissions.

Develop an internal audit program for compliance related tasks

Air Quality and Emissions Management

Provide technical oversight for emissions inventories, source testing, monitoring programs, and emissions calculations.

Evaluate operational and capital projects for permitting implications and environmental compliance impacts.

Coordinate with engineering and operations teams to identify permitting requirements associated with process modifications.

Maintain documentation supporting compliance with permit requirements and regulatory obligations.

Provide technical leadership for air permitting and regulatory applicability determinations, including BACT, NSR, PSD, and related permitting evaluations, to support business growth while maintaining environmental compliance.

Environmental Management Systems

Develop and maintain corporate environmental management systems (EMS).

Establish environmental metrics, KPIs, and performance indicators.

Support ISO 14001 implementation and continuous improvement initiatives.

Develop compliance calendars and audit protocols.

Maintain environmental records management systems and compliance tracking tools.

Sustainability and Stewardship

Support corporate sustainability initiatives and environmental performance improvement projects.

Identify opportunities to reduce emissions, waste generation, water usage, and overall environmental impact.

Assist with environmental data collection and reporting initiatives.

Partner with business leaders to support sustainability objectives and strategic environmental goals.

Act as point of contact for customer’s sustainability related requests

Training and Leadership

Develop and deliver environmental compliance training programs.

Participate in capital project reviews and Management of Change (MOC) processes.

Build a culture of environmental ownership and accountability throughout the organization.

Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the company and operational needs.

MINIMUM EDUCATION & WORK REQUIREMENTS: 

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Management, or a related field required; master’s degree preferred.

6+ years of progressive environmental compliance experience in manufacturing, food processing, agricultural processing, energy production, chemical processing, or other industrial environments.

Multi-site environmental management experience strongly preferred.

Demonstrated experience overseeing environmental permitting and regulatory compliance programs.

Experience working directly with environmental regulatory agencies and environmental consultants.

Preferred Certifications

Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM)

Certified Environmental Professional (CEP)

Professional Engineer (PE)

ISO 14001 Auditor Training

jobs.description:
Environmental Compliance Specialist I – NASA Glenn Research Center

Ready to take your environmental career to new heights? Join HSG in supporting NASA's mission!

We're looking for an Environmental Compliance Specialist to support environmental programs at NASA Glenn's Armstrong Test Facility in Ohio. This is a great opportunity to gain hands-on experience across hazardous waste management, stormwater, wastewater, spill prevention, and environmental compliance while contributing to the important work happening at NASA.

If you're passionate about environmental protection, enjoy hands-on problem-solving, and are ready to make an impact, we'd love to hear from you! Apply today and take the next step in your career with HSG!

General Description

Herndon Solutions Group (HSG) is seeking an Environmental Compliance Specialist I to serve as the on-site, multi-media environmental compliance resource at the NASA Glenn Research Center Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility (GRC-ATF) in Erie County, Ohio. The Specialist administers day-to-day compliance coordination across hazardous and regulated waste; petroleum, oil, and lubricant (POL) and tanks; spill preparedness and response; and stormwater and wastewater. The position evaluates site conditions, integrates requirements across environmental media, supports functional-area leads with inspections, field work, sampling, records, and reporting, and tracks ATF compliance issues through resolution. The Specialist supports Lewis Field when cross-site workload or continuity needs arise and reports to the designated HSG Project Manager/Site Lead. 

How You Will Fulfill Your Mission

Conduct and document environmental compliance inspections of hazardous and universal waste accumulation areas, used oil, POL/tanks, stormwater systems, wastewater operations, construction activities, and other assigned areas.
Serve as the primary on-site lead for the environmental compliance program for regulated waste, POL/tank, spills, stormwater, and wastewater, including permit requirements, inspections, monitoring, recordkeeping, deliverables, and corrective actions to identify compliance risks, recommend priorities, and support program improvements. 
Identify deficiencies, communicate findings, and recommend corrective actions based on an evaluation of regulatory significance, environmental risk, and operational impact. 
Support regulated and controlled waste management activities at ATF, including generator coordination, waste determinations, accumulation-area management, shipment documentation, sampling coordination, and cradle-to-grave recordkeeping including evaluation of waste characterization information and recommendations concerning appropriate management and disposal approaches. 
Support Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC), spill prevention, and POL/tank programs through inspections, inventory verification, spill response guide updates, alarm and event documentation, closure or maintenance support, and corrective-action tracking. 
Maintain ATF spill readiness and response activities, including initial assessments, containment coordination, sampling, waste management, documentation, reporting support, and post-incident follow-up. 
Support stormwater and wastewater permit compliance through site inspections, outfall screening, wet- and dry-weather monitoring, construction and post-construction best management practice (BMP) inspections, sampling coordination, discharge monitoring data reviews, equipment checks, reporting inputs, and maintenance of applicable plans and records.
Coordinate with laboratories and functional-area leads on field sampling plans, chain of custody, data quality, analytical results, and follow-up actions. 
Assist with identifying recurring compliance issues, evaluating potential environmental risks, and recommending practical improvements to procedures and environmental controls.
Support environmental audits, regulatory inspections, investigations, emergency drills, project reviews, meetings, and field activities, providing accurate ATF records and site knowledge. 
Coordinate closely with the Hazardous Waste Specialists at Lewis Field and the applicable waste, POL, stormwater, wastewater, and spill response functional leads to ensure consistent practices across both GRC locations. 
Track assigned environmental compliance issues and corrective actions through closure, escalating potential compliance concerns and matters requiring specialist review, Government approval, or regulatory coordination to the appropriate personnel.
Support emergency spill response activities at Lewis Field and ATF on an on-call/as needed basis and as coordinated by the Site Lead.

Why We Value You

You are able to work independently and show a high level of initiative and attention to detail.
You have a consistent character and do not yield to pressure to compromise or cut corners.
You have a strong ability to communicate effectively with superiors, colleagues, and customers by clearly expressing your intent and understanding the focus and purpose of the conversation while allowing each person to get their point across.
You are open to new ideas and innovations and can create modifications or changes in yourself to adapt or suit a new environment/situation.
You have faith in your own ideas and ability to be successful.
You hold yourself to the highest standard and work to inspire your team to produce quality work.

Specific Knowledge/Certification Requirements

Minimum Qualifications

Experience in environmental compliance, regulatory documentation, environmental monitoring, or related technical activities, including the ability to evaluate technical information and identify potential compliance concerns.
RCRA Hazardous Waste Management training and required refreshers or the ability to obtain prior to beginning field work.
DOT Hazardous Materials Ground Shipper training and required refreshers. 
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training and required refreshers. 
A Valid driver’s license and ability to obtain and maintain required NASA facility access. 

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, chemistry, biology, geology, occupational safety, or related discipline. 
Three or more years of multi-media environmental compliance experience at an industrial, research, aerospace, government, or similarly regulated facility. 
Experience with Ohio EPA requirements, NPDES permits, SPCC requirements, RCRA generator standards, construction stormwater controls, and environmental data and reporting systems. 
Ohio BUSTR Class A/B or Class C operator training, stormwater inspection credentials, or other applicable media-specific qualifications. 

Working Conditions

This is primarily an on-site position at the designated reporting location, with routine support at the other GRC location as operational needs require, including local travel between GRC-ATF and Lewis Field. 
Supports GRC core business hours. 
Must be able to work independently at GRC-ATF, including at remote site locations. 
Work may be performed in office, laboratory, industrial, warehouse, utility, construction, outdoor, and active facility environments. 
Must be able to lift, carry, or move 30 pounds or more; climb stairs; bend, stoop, twist, and reach; and stand or walk for two hours or more at one time. 
Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment and work in varying weather and site conditions. 
Conducts field inspections and sampling and provides limited hands-on support when needed to evaluate or coordinate compliance. Such work is incidental to the position’s primary compliance-administration duties. 
Must be able to participate in assigned emergency readiness and response coverage, including after-hours support when required.

Join Us! CDM Smith – where amazing career journeys unfold.

Imagine a place committed to offering an unmatched employee experience. Where you work on projects that are meaningful to you. Where you play an active part in shaping your career journey. Where your co-workers are invested in you and your success. Where you are encouraged and supported to do your very best and given the tools and resources to do so. Our employees are the heart of our company. As an employer of choice, our goal is to provide a challenging, progressive and inclusive work environment which fosters personal leadership, career growth and development for every employee. We value passionate individuals who challenge the norm, deliver world-class solutions and bring diverse perspectives. Join our team, and together we will make a difference and change the world.

Job Description

We are seeking an Environmental Scientist/Environmental Risk Assessor to support Human Health and Ecological projects for the Environmental Services Group. This candidate will primarily assist with regulatory compliance efforts for federal, state, and local environmental projects in CDM Smith’s portfolio.

Roles and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

With general direction, supports site investigations and basic to high complexity analysis and interpretation of site data relevant to human health risk assessments (HHRAs) and ecological risk assessments (ERAs).
Supports human health and ecological risk teams and contributes to the process of project tasks, including development of data quality objectives (DQOs), Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs), and sampling and analysis plans (SAPs).
With general direction, supports planning for and preparation of conceptual site exposure models (CSEMs), Human Health Risk Assessments (HHRAs), Screening Level Ecological Risk Assessments (SLERAs), and Baseline Ecological Risk Assessments (BERAs) of basic to high complexity.
Collaborates with scientists, geologists, engineers, and toxicologists to provide advice and expertise on the selected project approach, and to implement the approved approach (e.g., investigation, remediation, etc.).
On oversight projects, provides technical evaluation of responsible party’s project documents and supports technical meetings with clients and responsible parties.
Provides technical guidance and training to more junior staff and mentors them for future growth within the discipline and firm.
Collaborates with sales staff to support proposals in response to current and potential client requests for proposal (RFPs).
Contributes to firm's technical knowledge by developing white papers on emerging environmental issues.
Attends and presents at conferences, symposia, and other scientific venues to improve the visibility of the firm's products and services in collaboration with applicable sales staff.
Performs other duties as required.

Skills & Abilities

Expert Knowledge of standard field protocols for their respective discipline.
Expert knowledge of scientific methods and processes.
Expert Knowledge of Microsoft business software (excel, word, etc.).
Excellent verbal and written communications skills.
Expert knowledge of regulations (federal, state, and local) governing environmental review and project implementation.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Science or related discipline with professional scientist registration/certification OR Master's degree in Science or related discipline.
7 years of related experience.
Domestic and/or international travel may be required. The frequency of travel is contingent on specific duties, responsibilities, and the essential functions of the position, which may vary depending on workload and project demands.
Equivalent additional directly related experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in toxicology, environmental science, chemistry, public health, or related disciplines desired with a minimum of seven years of experience in environmental consulting, regulation or a similar environmental field.
Experience with various contaminant classes including (but not limited to) volatile organic compounds (VOCs), metals, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), radionuclides, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).
Experience with software/digital tools including (but not limited to) the Integrated Exposure Uptake Biokinetic (IEUBK) model, adult lead methodology (ALM) model; U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Regional Screening Level (RSL), Vapor Intrusion Screening Level (VISL), and Radionuclide Preliminary Remediation Goal (PRG) calculator tools; Biotic Ligand Model; Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) EcoRisk database, etc.
Familiarity with Remedial Investigation/Feasibility Study (RI/FS) requirements and guidance under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA), as well as other state-based programs (e.g., California Department of Toxic Substances Control [DTSC], District Department of the Environment [DDOE]).
Experience supporting clients directly in meetings resolving issues with responsible parties
Experience specific to contaminated sediment sites is desired.

10% or less

Job Description

The environment we live in has a huge impact on our health. Think about it. Is the air we breathe clean? Is the water contaminated? How will temperature and moisture levels affect the growth of toxic molds? It is for these reasons, along with myriad others, that the Army National Guard needs Environmental Scientists to join our team of Medical Corps Officers. But you won't stand apart from these heroes. You will stand among them as a commissioned Medical Corps Officer in the Army National Guard. Company Overview

Broadbent is an environmental remediation, water resources, and civil engineering firm founded in 1987. The firm serves energy companies, mining operations, municipalities, developers, and government agencies throughout the United States. Broadbent provides practical, cost-effective solutions supported by technical expertise and responsive client service.

Primary Responsibilities

Manage environmental assessment, investigation, and remediation projects from proposal development through regulatory closure.
Prepare project scopes, proposals, cost estimates, work plans, schedules, and budgets.

Prepare and review investigation reports, corrective action plans, remediation work plans, monitoring reports, regulatory correspondence, and closure requests.
Develop and refine conceptual site models (CSMs) using site history, field observations, analytical results, geology, hydrogeology, and contaminant distribution.
Manage project scope, schedule, budget, invoicing, subcontractors, and deliverables.
Serve as a primary client contact and communicate project status, findings, regulatory requirements, and recommendations.
Mentor junior staff and provide technical direction related to field activities, data evaluation, and report preparation.
Support business development through client relationship management.

Minimum Qualifications

Current Nevada Certified Environmental Manager (CEM) preferred. Candidates licensed as a Professional Geologist (PG) or Registered Geologist (RG) must be eligible and willing to obtain a Nevada CEM within the first year of employment.

Experience developing project scopes, cost estimates, proposals, technical reports, schedules, budgets, and Nevada Petroleum Fund documentation.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects while meeting scope, schedule, budget, and deliverable requirements.
Strong technical writing, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills.
