We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The strategic professional we seek is a motivated individual with these qualifications.

Doctorate degree and 2 years of marketing and/or business experience in a role aligned with a Marketing/Sales commercial organization; OR

Master's degree and 4 years of marketing and/or business experience in a role aligned with a Marketing/Sales commercial organization; OR

Bachelor's degree and 6 years of marketing and/or business experience in a role aligned with a Marketing/Sales commercial organization; OR

Associate's degree and 10 years of marketing and/or business experience in a role aligned with a Marketing/Sales commercial organization; OR

Preferred Qualifications

MBA or other advanced degree preferred.

Demonstrated direct people-management experience, including coaching and developing talent, setting priorities, and leading through change.

Strong Medical Marketing, OL engagement, and P2P expertise, including OL mapping and engagement planning, Speaker Bureau operations, speaker training, marketing-led HCP education, promotional content development, and multichannel education.

Experience leading P2P and marketing-led OL/HCP engagements end-to-end, including congress-based programs, speaker strategy, faculty management, program design, agency/vendor management, budget oversight, performance optimization, and MAC review through systems such as Veeva PromoMats.

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. What You’ll Be Doing…

The Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) team is a part of VBG. This role will be responsible for leading c ross-segment integrated marketing strategies and programs that would include initiatives touching Enterprise, Public Sector, and/or Business Markets across the CMO and Verizon Business Group. You will focus on marketing strategy, execution, performance management, and go-to-market plans relative to product launches, campaign pivots, and product promotions.

In this role, you will work in lockstep with Product Marketing, Demand Gen, CRM, Media, Creative, and Digital/Dotcom teams to build integrated programs in support of our Wireline Business. You will own internal communication of local campaign progress to all stakeholders, agency briefings, and GTM kickoffs while ensuring flawless execution. Additionally, you will serve as a flexible, agile contributor on the team, taking on other key IMC initiatives and special projects as business needs evolve. In this role, you will report to an Associate Director within the IMC segment team.

The IMC Senior Manager will lead the planning, briefing, management, execution, creative optimization, and reporting on Wireline multi-channel campaigns that drive to the sale funnel or direct to digital channels, increase awareness,and build long-term business relationships. You will have the authority and independence to ensure that requirements, communication opportunities, and risks are identified, managed, and completed in a timely fashion to achieve on-time completion of key deliverables.

Collaborating in lockstep with Product Marketing to define campaign objectives, align on strategies, and establish baseline briefs.
Partnering closely with the Media team to monitor campaign performance, track KPIs/GAs, and optimize local/regional media plans.
Working closely with Creative teams and agencies to analyze performance data and execute real-time creative pivots, A/B testing, and message testing when applicable.
Owning and managing the digital and Dotcom integration for your initiatives—ensuring seamless user journeys, landing page alignment, appointment-booking functionality, and strong cross-functional digital execution.
Authoring, owning, and presenting strategic briefs, local pilot presentations, and deck updates for multiple LOBs and leadership stakeholders.
Synthesizing media performance and local event ROI (GAs, leads, engagement) to share regular results, updates, and strategic recommendations out to leadership.
Managing complex, multi-faceted timelines with exceptional organizational skills to ensure all deliverables stay on strategy and on deadline.
Leading and supporting additional high-priority IMC initiatives and cross-functional projects outside of Wireline marketing as needed by the business.
Maintaining a deep understanding of market dynamics, competitive threats, and emerging trends to fill knowledge gaps and refine marketing strategy.

What We're Looking For…

You’ll need to have:

Bachelor’s degree or four or more years of work experience.
Six or more years of relevant experience required, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training.
Experience working cross-functionally across Digital/Dotcom, Field Sales/Marketing, Product Marketing, and/or Media teams.
B2B Marketing experience.
Experience creating and presenting executive-level decks, performance readouts, and strategic briefs to Sr. Director-level leadership and above.
Experience translating market insights and data into compelling stories and sales enablement tools.

Even better if you have one or more of the following:

Master’s degree; preferably MBA.
Marketing experience in Wireline marketing, targeting Enterprise customers and prospects.
Experience working closely with Media and Creative teams to evaluate live campaign metrics and execute iterative creative pivots.
Strong organizational skills and proven ability to juggle multiple complex, cross-functional initiatives simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
Experience using generative AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or Copilot) to streamline workflows, enhance productivity, and support decision-making.

Proven digital/Dotcom marketing background with a solid understanding of web journeys, lead conversion pathways, and digital trends.
Strong project management background with high attention to detail and process optimization.
Agile mindset with the ability to easily adapt and step in on high-visibility adjacent projects.
Must be a team player and highly effective communicator capable of building strong cross-functional relationships.

40

jobs.title: Director of Marketing and Social
jobs.description:
Full Time | Portland, OR | Primarily in office with hybrid flexibility
Reports to: Chief of Staff and President
ABOUT COLLiDE

COLLiDE brings sports, culture and community together through the Portland Pickles, Lake County Captains, Portland Bangers, Portland Cherry Bombs FC and Official League apparel. Our teams have distinct personalities, and we want our marketing to give people a reason to follow us, come to a game and be part of what we are building.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a creative leader to own social media strategy, content direction and audience growth across our teams. You will help our staff develop better ideas, grow our accounts and turn social attention into ticket and merchandise campaigns.

You should understand what makes people stop scrolling, keep watching, share a post and follow an account. You will bring that knowledge into creative reviews, campaign planning and coaching, with clear expectations for quality, timing and results.

Your primary focus will be our four sports teams, with broader strategic support for Official League. You will manage approximately 2–3 direct reports and support a wider group of 5–8 staff. You will assign work, approve campaigns and help the existing team execute. Our advertising team will continue running paid ads, working from a coordinated campaign strategy.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead social media strategy and content

Own the social media strategy for each team, including Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook and YouTube. Set clear goals and tailor content to the audience and platform.
Lead creative reviews of concepts, hooks, captions, short videos and campaigns. Make curiosity a starting point and give people a reason to watch, share or participate.
Guide content planning, approvals and production timelines. Keep planned campaigns moving while leaving room to respond quickly to trends and cultural moments.
Study our strongest past posts and campaigns, understand why they worked and adapt those lessons while keeping each team's voice distinct.

Grow audiences and engagement

Build campaigns and recurring content that bring in new followers and keep existing fans involved throughout the year.
Set expectations for engaging with fans, responding to comments and messages, and joining relevant conversations. Build relationships with brands, creators and community accounts that can help us reach new people.
Review follower growth, reach, views, watch time, shares and comments. Identify what deserves another test, what to improve and what to stop.

Lead and support our staff

Give staff clear priorities, useful feedback and achievable deadlines. Hold regular check-ins, help remove obstacles and follow up on commitments.
Teach the strategy behind effective social content and campaigns. Encourage new ideas and help people develop their judgment and skills.
Coordinate with property GMs and department leaders so staff have the information, assets and support they need to deliver.

Turn social campaigns into sales

Work with ticketing and merchandise staff to build social campaigns around product launches, ticket offers, promotions and renewals.
Connect social content with email, websites, paid advertising and partner promotion. Set the audience, message, offer and timing before launch.
Track which campaigns generate interest, leads and purchases. Use the results to improve our approach and make good use of staff time and available budgets.

WHAT YOU BRING

At least 5 years of relevant marketing experience, including substantial responsibility for social media strategy and managing staff.
Examples of social accounts you helped grow and campaigns you personally led. Be ready to explain the creative idea, your role and the results.
Strong practical knowledge of social platforms, content formats, audience behavior and performance measurement. You keep learning as platforms and habits change.
A strong understanding of marketing strategy and how social content supports ticket sales, merchandise and long-term fan relationships.
Experience coaching people, giving direct feedback and holding a team accountable while supporting their growth.
The ability to turn an idea into a realistic plan, make timely decisions and work within available resources.
An open mind, strong creative judgment and willingness to test new ideas and challenge your own assumptions. Experience in sports, entertainment, live events or consumer brands is helpful.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Our social accounts are growing, reaching new people and giving fans reasons to engage and return.
Our content reflects each team's personality, creates curiosity and responds to opportunities while they still matter.
Staff have clear direction, improve their work and deliver campaigns on time with consistent support and accountability.
Social campaigns support ticket and merchandise sales, and we understand which efforts are working.

LOCATION AND BENEFITS

This role is based primarily in our Portland office, with hybrid flexibility and travel to Northeast Ohio and other COLLiDE markets.
Benefits include health insurance contributions, paid time off, merchandise discounts and lots of free tickets. 

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

jobs.description:
About the Role and Why It Is A Little Different

Most marketing leadership ads want a one-person band. This one wants a conductor. We have a bench of specialist contractors, each a real expert in their own lane, spread worldwide. They need a leader who sets priorities, writes a clear brief, clears roadblocks, and knows great work when they see it.

Your mission: keep people coordinated, projects moving, deadlines visible, and results measurable. You do not need to be an expert in every marketing channel. You do need to be good at managing the experts who are.
If you enjoy managing many moving parts and turning them into a plan—and a plan into completed work—we should talk.

We are seeking a senior In-House Marketing Director to orchestrate our multi-channel growth engine. In this role, you will serve as the operational quarterback—managing specialized freelance contributors. You will set the creative brief, enforce brand/legal compliance for consistent messaging, audit contractor output, and execute and scale multi-channel acquisition and brand-awareness campaigns. In this role, you will bridge legal/tax expertise with high-impact digital marketing to grow B2C and B2B leads, dominate local search footprints, and produce authority-building content across video, webinar, and social channels.

You will work closely with leadership, our established LinkedIn marketing team, and various freelancers to turn specialized tax-bankruptcy thought leadership into measurable new leads.

About Tax Workout Group

Tax Workout Group is a growing national law firm focused on tax controversy and tax-motivated bankruptcy. We have expanded our office footprint and want to invest in a coordinated marketing operation to support the firm’s growth. We operate as a lean business, so we’re building our marketing team differently: one full-time leader coordinating a distributed network of specialist contractors. We rely on talented people who know their craft, and we need someone who can help them work together effectively.

We have one full-time marketing seat, and it is a leadership position. You will plan, assign, track, unblock, and evaluate the work of a distributed team, and you will be accountable for the results. Your marketing knowledge makes you good at it, but managing people and projects is the job.

Lead the team

Recruit, onboard, evaluate, and (when needed) replace contractors, mainly through Upwork and similar platforms
Turn marketing goals into clear, well-scoped briefs that a remote specialist can pick up and run with
Run several projects at once: set priorities, sequence the work, manage dependencies, and keep every workstream moving
Give specific, kind feedback, and hold people accountable for quality, deadlines, and results

Direct marketing and software projects

Oversee work across the lanes listed below, each carried out by the specialists who own it
Guide development of the custom, web-hosted marketing software we build and use, from requirements through release
Keep one current, honest view of status, risks, and deadlines for firm leadership

Measure, report, and stay compliant

Use analytics to judge both campaign performance and contractor performance
Deliver a consolidated monthly report of marketing spend across contractors, tools, and other expenses
Keep all marketing work in line with Florida Bar advertising rules

Stay hands-on where it’s quick

Handle small ad hoc requests that take five minutes instead of a day to write up for someone else. We love this, but it’s a bonus, not the job.

The Lanes Your Specialists Own

You’ll know each one well enough to set sound goals, ask good questions, tell great work from so-so work, and notice when a deadline has quietly wandered off.

Local office marketing (map and directory listings)
Social media, business-to-consumer
Social media, business-to-business
Email marketing
Webinars (event marketing)
Video marketing (YouTube, TikTok, and video embedded in other channels)
Public relations (primarily press releases)
Reputation management (soliciting and responding to customer reviews)
Organic SEO and content marketing
Paid search advertising
Measurement, reporting, and analytics

What We’re Looking For - Project management comes first.
We’re looking for someone with experience managing multiple projects at once, coordinating multiple contributors, and delivering results.

You should bring:
Demonstrated experience managing projects, priorities, deadlines, and deliverables.
Experience coordinating remote contractors, freelancers, or distributed teams.
Strong delegation, written communication, follow-through, and problem-solving skills.
Enough marketing-generalist knowledge to understand what specialists are doing, evaluate their work, and ask intelligent questions.
Comfort with project management tools, performance metrics, budgets, and status reporting.
The ability to work independently, make sound decisions, and bring structure to an evolving operation.
Flexibility for occasional meetings outside conventional business hours.

Especially valuable experience

Experience managing software development projects, marketing projects, multiple teams, parallel projects, remote contributors, and international teams
would be particularly valuable.
Law firm marketing experience, familiarity with digital marketing analytics, and practical use of generative AI tools are additional pluses.

What You Don’t Need to Be - You do not need to personally run every ad campaign, write every article, edit every video, or become the world’s leading authority on all things SEO. You do need to know enough to manage the people who handle those tasks, and it helps to be able to knock out a quick task yourself when that’s more efficient.

What Success Looks Like - Our contractors know what to do. Projects don’t disappear into the void. Deadlines and budgets are managed. Problems surface early. Marketing initiatives move forward in parallel, and management can see results.

Work Location and Employment
Fully remote:
Work from your home office.
US-based applicants only.

Full-time employment.

Ready to Apply?
Tell us about your experience managing projects, coordinating remote contractors, and getting results through a team. Concrete examples of projects you’ve successfully delivered are especially helpful. We’re looking for a thoughtful, organized, proactive leader who enjoys making complicated things work better. If you can bring order to a dozen moving parts without becoming one more moving part yourself, we’d love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
About Telnyx

Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. From architecting and amplifying the reach of a private, global, multi-cloud IP network , to bringing hyperlocal edge technology right to your fingertips through intuitive APIs, we're shaping a new era of seamless interconnection between people, devices, and applications.

We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team.

Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.

Who you are

A demand generation operator who runs marketing like an engineering system: you plan, execute, measure and iterate with AI agents doing the heavy mechanics and you making the judgment calls. You own outcomes, not channels. You are joining a small, Demand Gen team where every member owns a product pod end-to-end; yours is a brand-new pod that you build from zero, with dedicated budget.

What you'll do

Run paid media across every channel we operate. Launch and manage campaigns across search, social, programmatic and emerging AI ad surfaces. You run the whole loop yourself, per channel and per region: launch QA, pacing, creative refresh and landing page validation.
Direct the AI agent fleet. Our campaign operations run on autonomous agents built on agentic runtimes like Hermes and powered by frontier models like Claude. They propose budget shifts, copy fixes, and keyword and audience changes. You write and refine the prompts, review recommendations with confidence scores, run the approval queue, and decide when to override the machine. You get more done through agents than through dashboards.
Own the budget. Monthly budget planning and pacing across platforms, reallocations grounded in performance data, spend tracking you can defend line by line, and discipline inside approval guardrails.
Optimize relentlessly. Weekly performance reviews across all channels, creative fatigue detection, search term and audience mining, CPA and funnel diagnostics, kill/scale decisions with pre-declared thresholds.
Run ABM end-to-end. Define the pod's ICP and target account lists, build ABM segments and Salesforce pools, run regional rollouts with sales, and keep lists clean and synced with ad platforms.
Close the alignment loop. You are the bridge between sales, RevOps and product marketing: hot accounts and win/loss reviews with sales, lead routing and attribution with RevOps, positioning and messaging with PMM. You feed paid-media intelligence back into all three.
Run influencer and creator programs. Identify, brief and amplify creators; manage sponsorship and paid amplification of their content; measure whether their audiences actually convert.
Report to stakeholders. Weekly and monthly performance reporting to sales, marketing and leadership, in plain language with honest numbers and clear next steps.

What we're looking for

5+ years in B2B demand generation for developer tools, infrastructure, telecom or a comparable technical category
Hands-on, full-funnel paid media experience across at least three major ad platforms
AI and agentic fluency is the core requirement: you already use AI agents or automation in your marketing work, you can prompt precisely, review machine-generated recommendations critically, and design workflows where humans approve and machines execute
ABM experience with concrete examples of account targeting that produced pipeline
Strong with data: you can reconcile platform-reported conversions against CRM and attribution data and say no to numbers that don't hold up
Comfortable owning a new, undefined space: budget arrives, the motion gets built

What's in it for you

You work at the edge of AI and the infrastructure that powers it. The products you market are the same ones you use: AI agents, agentic runtimes and Telnyx's own inference APIs sit inside your daily workflow, not behind a vendor roadmap.
You get the latest tooling before anyone else. Frontier models, agent frameworks, voice AI and inference: you run the newest AI tools as part of the job, and your feedback shapes how they ship.
You build from zero with an unfair head start. A dedicated pod budget, an agent fleet already executing the mechanics, and senior counterparts who run the other pods end-to-end.
You own a real budget. You decide where the money goes, and you are measured on pipeline, activations and revenue, not vanity dashboards.

jobs.title: Senior Funnel & Marketing Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Funnel & Marketing Systems Engineer
Launch OS Marketing

ABOUT LAUNCH OS MARKETING

Launch OS Marketing helps high-ticket businesses scale through performance marketing, conversion-focused funnels, and reliable marketing systems.

We’re building something big, and we’re looking for A players who want to help build it—people who take pride in their work, bring ideas to the table, and take ownership of results.

If your goal is simply to clock in, complete assigned tasks, and clock out, this role won’t be the right fit. We want someone who identifies opportunities, solves problems, communicates proactively, and follows through.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Senior Funnel & Marketing Systems Engineer owns the technical journey from ad click to application, booked call, follow-up, and recorded sale.

You’ll turn approved copy, offer direction, and client assets into polished, conversion-focused funnels. You’ll also build and maintain the CRM workflows, integrations, attribution, and dashboards behind them.

This is a hands-on role spanning both frontend execution and backend systems. You should be equally comfortable improving a mobile page layout, diagnosing a broken integration, and verifying that a sales dashboard reflects accurate numbers.

You’ll manage technical delivery across six to eight clients, balancing new builds, onboarding projects, ongoing improvements, and maintenance.

You own the complete, tested result—not just your portion of the task list.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Build conversion-focused funnels. Develop landing pages, sales pages, applications, booking flows, checkout flows, and supporting pages for DSL/VSL, webinar, challenge, quiz, advertorial, free-training, and low-to-high-ticket ascension funnels.
• Own design and frontend execution. Translate approved copy and client assets into intentional layouts with strong typography, spacing, visual hierarchy, and clear calls to action. Build responsive experiences using platform tools and custom HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
• Build and maintain GoHighLevel and HubSpot systems. Configure forms, custom fields, pipelines, qualification logic, lead routing, sales assignments, calendars, and lifecycle stages.
• Develop email and SMS automations. Build nurture, booking, reminder, no-show, follow-up, and reactivation workflows with appropriate triggers, branches, timing, and stopping conditions.
• Connect the tools behind the funnel. Implement integrations through Zapier, APIs, webhooks, and tools such as SendBlue. Maintain accurate field mappings, prevent duplicate actions, and troubleshoot failed transfers.
• Implement attribution and conversion tracking. Support primarily Meta-driven acquisition by preserving campaign information, validating conversion events, and connecting marketing activity to CRM outcomes.
• Build sales and attribution dashboards. Provide visibility into leads, qualified applications, bookings, attendance, sales, ad spend, and collected revenue. Define metrics clearly and reconcile reporting against source records.
• Own quality control. Test the customer journey, page behavior, data flow, and automation logic before handoff. Verify that systems continue working after launch.
• Manage delivery proactively. Scope work, provide realistic estimates, track dependencies, and communicate progress, blockers, and capacity concerns early.
• Improve how we build. Create reusable components, documented workflows, checklists, and processes that increase speed and reliability across client accounts.

REQUIREMENTS

• Demonstrated experience building and maintaining direct-response funnels for high-ticket businesses.
• Strong hands-on experience in GoHighLevel and HubSpot, including their workflows, CRM structures, and integration capabilities.
• Strong HTML, CSS, and JavaScript skills for custom layouts, responsive behavior, forms, and troubleshooting.
• Strong visual judgment. You understand spacing, typography, hierarchy, and consistency, and can produce polished pages without needing a detailed mockup for every build.
• Practical understanding of conversion rate optimization, including message continuity, credibility, form friction, and clear next steps.
• Experience with APIs, webhooks, JSON, authentication, and field mapping, including investigating failed or duplicated data transfers.
• Experience implementing attribution and building dashboards that connect marketing activity with sales outcomes.
• A repeatable process for testing, documentation, and quality control.
• The ability to prioritize across multiple clients and manage competing deadlines.
• Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining technical issues to nontechnical teammates.
• Experience using Codex, Claude Code, or comparable AI development tools effectively.

Our standard for automation is simple:

If you don’t know how to do something manually, you cannot automate it.

You must understand the underlying process, explain the logic you implement, and troubleshoot the systems you build. We expect you to use modern tools effectively and take responsibility for everything you ship.

QUALITY STANDARDS

Quality control is part of the build. Before handing work over, you should have checked:

• Desktop and mobile layouts, spacing, typography, links, and calls to action.
• Forms, validation, submissions, bookings, and checkouts where applicable.
• Field mappings, qualification rules, pipeline stages, and owner assignments.
• Workflow branches, delays, re-entry, and duplicate submissions.
• Messaging eligibility and stopping conditions after bookings, replies, or opt-outs.
• Attribution data, conversion events, and reporting accuracy.
• Failure handling and recovery for unsuccessful integrations.

You should be able to show what you tested, what passed, and what still needs attention.

EXPECTED RESULTS

• Polished funnels: Pages look intentional, work across devices, and require minimal avoidable rework.
• Reliable launches: Builds meet agreed requirements and timelines, with risks communicated early.
• Dependable automations: Leads reach the correct destination, follow-up reflects their current status, and failures are visible and recoverable.
• Accurate reporting: Dashboards use clearly defined metrics and numbers that reconcile with underlying records.
• Clear communication: The Growth Marketing Manager and CMO know what is complete, what is next, and what needs a decision.
• Stronger processes: Reusable systems and documentation improve delivery speed and reduce recurring mistakes.
• Proactive improvement: You identify issues and opportunities before someone has to assign them to you.

CORE VALUES

Extreme Ownership
Take responsibility for the outcome. Clarify expectations, follow through, and own the resolution when something goes wrong.

Initiative and Resourcefulness
Investigate unfamiliar problems, consult documentation, test your assumptions, and bring a recommended solution.

High Standards
Care about the details. Check your work thoroughly and take pride in delivering something the team can trust.

Clear, Direct Communication
Give honest updates, raise concerns early, and explain tradeoffs clearly. Speak up when you see a better approach.

Speed With Discipline
Move with urgency while protecting the quality of the result. Build efficient processes that reduce rework.

Continuous Improvement
Seek feedback, sharpen your skills, and turn lessons into better systems for the entire team.

SCHEDULE

• 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Mountain Time.
• Availability to support critical launches or events when needed.
• Proactive communication around priorities, deadlines, and availability.

LOCATION AND EMPLOYMENT TYPE

• Fully remote, United States.
• Full-time employee position.

REPORTING

This role reports to the Growth Marketing Manager and CMO and works closely with the team responsible for client strategy and delivery.

COMPENSATION

• $95,000–$110,000 USD annual base salary, based on experience.
• Revenue-share bonus tied to your assigned pod of clients.

The revenue-share structure and payout terms will be discussed during the hiring process.

BENEFITS

• Paid time off.
• Company-wide paid holidays.
• $3,000 annual investment budget for tools, resources, and gear that support your work and professional growth.

HOW TO APPLY

Please submit:

1. A two-to-five-minute Loom introduction. Introduce yourself, describe your current or most recent position, explain what you personally owned and were responsible for, and tell us what you’re looking for in your next role.
2. Two relevant funnel examples. Explain your contribution to the design, development, backend, and tracking. Redacted walkthroughs are welcome where client work is confidential.
3. One automation or integration example. Describe the problem, the systems involved, the logic you built, and how you verified it worked.
4. A brief explanation of your quality-control process. Include a checklist or example if available.
5. Your availability and potential start date.

Shortlisted applicants will complete a paid practical assessment and live technical review focused on funnel execution, automation, troubleshooting, and quality control.

We want to see how you think, how you build, and how you prove your work is ready.

Marketing Event and Administrative Coordinator (Temporary)

LOCATION AND WORK MODEL

Extent of responsibility:
Regional.

A collaborative and innovative work environment.

WORK AUTHORIZATION

AI ASSISTED APPLICATION MATERIALS

Applications that include fabricated or exaggerated experience, hidden text or embedded instructions, or prescreen responses that do not reflect your own knowledge may be removed from consideration. jobs.title: Manager, Marketing Data & Analytics
jobs.description:
Are you a dreamer, innovator, thinker and a do-er who believes in contributing to something that makes difference?

Make an impact. Join PMI.

How will you make a difference to PMI?

The Manager, Marketing Data and Analytics owns the business data architecture and metric definitions behind Marketing's numbers, and leads the team that measures Marketing. The role defines how marketing, customer, product, and revenue data should be modeled, decides what each metric means, and ensures those definitions are implemented consistently across Snowflake, BI, and natural-language analytics.

The role combines hands-on technical depth with team leadership. The individual is expected to be advanced in SQL, to design analytical data models, and to profile, reconcile, and diagnose data directly, so they can specify what engineering builds and verify that the result represents the business correctly. They are equally expected to lead three to four analysts, set the standards those analysts work to, and develop the team's technical capability.

Data Engineering and the Snowflake team own ingestion, infrastructure, orchestration, transformation pipelines, and semantic view implementation. This role represents Marketing in the design of the data layer, writes the specifications those teams build against, and is accountable for ensuring the resulting data products correctly represent the business.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

Business Data Architecture, Metric Definitions, and Context

Own Marketing's canonical metric definitions and the business logic the governed semantic layer implements, and arbitrate those definitions when marketing, finance, and reporting platforms disagree.
Specify the semantic models for the most complex and cross-domain marketing use cases, and validate what the Snowflake team builds against that specification.
Own the business data architecture for Marketing, defining the facts, dimensions, grain, relationships, hierarchies, and conformed dimensions that connect marketing, customer, product, transaction, and engagement data.
Design analytical models that answer cross-domain questions spanning acquisition, engagement, conversion, certification, membership, renewal, and revenue.
Write advanced SQL to profile data, validate sources, reconcile metrics, build reusable datasets, and investigate complex customer and business questions.
Determine what unstructured content, such as business documentation, definitions, and prior analyses, must be retrievable alongside structured metrics for natural-language and agent-based analysis, and maintain source-to-metric mappings and lineage.
Own the business questions, expected results, and synonym glossary behind the Verified Query Repository supporting Cortex Analyst and natural-language analytics.
Own the context layer that makes Marketing's data interpretable to analysts and AI agents, including entity descriptions, metric documentation, approved analytical uses, and known limitations of each source.
Diagnose discrepancies across Snowflake, BI, Adobe Analytics, marketing platforms, finance reporting, and operational systems.
Identify gaps in source data, identity resolution, event structures, and dimensional consistency before they become downstream reporting issues.
Define ownership boundaries between source systems, engineered data products, semantic models, and reporting layers.

Team Leadership and Capability

Lead, coach, and develop a team of three to four analysts spanning paid media, customer and lifecycle analytics, and digital analytics.
Set the Marketing Analytics roadmap, allocate the team against it, and manage intake and prioritization from across Marketing.
Establish and enforce analytical standards including SQL quality, peer review, testing, documentation, and reuse.
Review the team's models, queries, and analyses before they reach stakeholders, and hold the quality bar for what gets published.
Grow the team's depth in dimensional modeling, data modeling practice, and analytical rigor through direct coaching and review.
Manage performance, hiring, and development planning for the team.

Marketing Measurement and Performance Analytics

Define and govern core marketing KPIs including revenue, conversion, CAC and CPA, ROAS, retention, funnel progression, pacing to plan, and channel efficiency.
Own the integrity and narrative of recurring executive performance reporting, including monthly business reviews and QBR analytics, with the team producing the underlying analysis.
Determine how platform-reported, attribution-based, financial, and incrementality-based measures reconcile, and establish where each is appropriately used.
Lead attribution, cohort, and incrementality work so it produces decision-grade guidance on marketing investment, building the harder analyses directly.
Own predictive modeling for Marketing, including membership churn and renewal propensity, certification lapse and recertification likelihood, and product and cross-sell propensity, alongside segmentation, lifecycle, and cohort analysis across CRM, web, campaign, commerce, certification, and membership data.
Define the features, target definitions, validation approach, and performance thresholds for predictive models, determine when a score is reliable enough to act on, and establish how scores are refreshed, monitored for drift, and activated in campaign, lifecycle, and retention programs.
Set analytical standards for A/B testing, holdouts, geo experiments, and conversion-lift studies within the marketing analytics practice, including hypotheses, test populations, success metrics, and readouts.
Partner with Product and Marketing to define measurable funnels, customer states, lifecycle stages, and behavioral signals for considered-purchase journeys, and hold a clear distinction between attribution, correlation, prediction, and causal measurement when results are communicated.

Analytics Delivery and Enablement

Govern Marketing's analytical products in enterprise BI and visualization platforms, ensuring definitions are sourced from the semantic layer rather than rebuilt in the tool.
Use Adobe Analytics to investigate digital behavior, traffic, customer journeys, and conversion performance, and work with data from Adobe Experience Platform, CRM, commerce, and paid media systems.
Apply working knowledge of digital event instrumentation, tagging, identity, and schemas to identify measurement and architecture issues at the source, and establish where AI-assisted tooling is applied to SQL development, analysis, documentation, and testing.
Expand governed self-service and AI-assisted analytics for Marketing across Snowflake, BI, and natural-language surfaces, and represent Marketing data and context requirements in the Marketing AI reference architecture.
Define what Marketing data and context AI agents and natural-language tools are permitted to reach, at what grain, and under what access and accuracy controls, and own the evaluation approach that tests answer accuracy before release and monitors it as data and definitions change.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Serve as Marketing's primary analytical counterpart to Data Engineering, Data Architecture, and Data Governance.
Translate business questions into analytical requirements and data-product specifications that engineering can build against.
Partner with Data Engineering on transformation logic, data contracts, source integration, model design, and data-quality requirements.
Partner with Performance Marketing, Brand, Digital, Product, Lifecycle, and Regional Marketing on measurement needs and analytical priorities.
Present analytical findings, performance trends, and recommendations to senior leadership.

Scope of Role

Leads a team of three to four analysts covering marketing, customer, and performance analytics, while personally designing analytical data models and validating them. Accountable for Marketing's business data architecture, metric definitions, context layer, predictive models, and executive performance reporting across certification, membership, e-learning, events, and other product lines.

Hands-on ownership concentrates in data model design, metric reconciliation, predictive model validation, evaluation of analytical accuracy, and diagnosis of cross-system discrepancies. Semantic view implementation sits with the Snowflake team, built to this role's specification. Routine reporting, campaign analysis, and dashboard production sit with the team, under this role's review and standards.

Data Engineering, Technology, and the Snowflake team own ingestion, infrastructure, orchestration, platform access, transformation pipelines, and semantic view implementation. Enterprise data governance policy, cataloging, and cross-domain stewardship sit outside this role; the incumbent partners with Data Governance and applies those standards within Marketing.

Role Qualifications

10+ years across marketing analytics, customer analytics, analytics engineering, or related disciplines, including prior leadership of an analytics team.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing an analytics team while remaining hands-on technically.
Working knowledge of ETL and ELT concepts, transformation pipelines, data dependencies, and data-quality controls, with the ability to read, review, and challenge logic developed by engineering teams.
Experience working within layered, dimensional, or medallion data architectures.
Experience integrating and analyzing data across CRM, marketing, digital, commerce, and transactional systems.
Development and governance of analytical products in an enterprise BI platform, preferred.
Customer data platform architecture including identity resolution, event schema design, and audience activation.
Marketing measurement including attribution, experimentation, incrementality, conversion, CAC and CPA, and ROAS, and experience directing or building predictive and propensity models such as churn or retention.

Collen is hiring a Marketing, Business Development & Administration Coordinator to support its growth teams. In short, this is a hybrid of bid support, marketing and office coordination. Above all, the role centres on prequalification submissions, which help a contractor qualify to tender for new projects. In addition, you will keep records accurate, organise meetings and events, and support senior stakeholders. Therefore, it suits an organised communicator who enjoys detail as much as variety.

About Collen And The Team

Collen is a long-established construction and engineering company, and it also operates outside Ireland, including in Sweden. Because the business competes for major projects, strong prequalification work has a direct impact on which contracts the company can bid for. As a result, this role sits at the point where marketing, data and new business meet.

In practice, you will work closely with directors, managers and several internal teams. For example, you will gather staff CVs, qualifications and performance data for submissions. Meanwhile, you will also prepare presentations and marketing materials, and you will help run company events, some of them international.

Responsibilities

Marketing and business development

Prepare prequalification applications and support related business development activities.
Maintain and update client databases and business development records.
Keep staff CVs, experience and qualification records ready for prequalification submissions.
Track prequalification performance data and prepare reports on it.
Maintain employee CPD records where required.
Develop marketing materials, presentations and company information.
Help organise and coordinate company marketing events.
Support the management of international events.

Administration and coordination

Provide day-to-day administrative support to directors, managers and teams.
Coordinate meetings, including scheduling, logistics, documents and minute-taking where required.
Prepare reports, presentations, correspondence and other business documents.
Maintain organised records, filing systems and document-control processes.
Manage calendars, appointments and meeting arrangements where required.
Handle confidential and business-sensitive information with discretion.
Support internal and external communications and stakeholder coordination.
Assist with general office administration and ad hoc tasks.

Minimum Qualifications

Previous experience in a marketing, business development or administrative support role.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Excellent organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritise competing demands.
A high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
The ability to work independently while collaborating with multiple stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

A qualification in Marketing, Communications, Business Administration or a related discipline.
Experience with CRM or document-management systems.

Beyond the skills above, Collen also looks for a professional, proactive and service-focused approach. Similarly, problem-solving, initiative and discretion with confidential information all matter in this role.

Salary and benefits

The advert does not state a salary range or any benefits . Likewise, it does not confirm the contract type, working hours or work model. Therefore, raise these points with Collen’s recruitment team early in the process.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ)

What are prequalification submissions in this role?

They are documents a contractor submits to show its capability before it can tender for a project. In this role, you will compile staff CVs, qualifications and performance data for them. Consequently, accuracy and good record-keeping are central to the job.

Do I need a marketing degree to apply?

No. Collen lists a qualification in Marketing, Communications or Business Administration as desirable, not essential. However, you do need previous experience in a marketing, business development or administrative support role.

Will this role involve travel?

Possibly. The advert mentions support for international event management, and Collen operates outside Ireland. Still, it does not say how much travel is involved

Experience working cross-functionally across Digital/Dotcom, Field Sales/Marketing, Product Marketing, and/or Media teams.
B2B Marketing experience.
Experience creating and presenting executive-level decks, performance readouts, and strategic briefs to Sr. Director-level leadership and above.
Experience translating market insights and data into compelling stories and sales enablement tools.

Master’s degree; preferably MBA.
Marketing experience in Wireline marketing, targeting Enterprise customers and prospects.
Experience working closely with Media and Creative teams to evaluate live campaign metrics and execute iterative creative pivots.
Strong organizational skills and proven ability to juggle multiple complex, cross-functional initiatives simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
Experience using generative AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or Copilot) to streamline workflows, enhance productivity, and support decision-making.
ABM/DBM/Content syndication experience.
Agency or consultant experience.
Proven digital/Dotcom marketing background with a solid understanding of web journeys, lead conversion pathways, and digital trends.
Strong project management background with high attention to detail and process optimization.
Agile mindset with the ability to easily adapt and step in on high-visibility adjacent projects.
Must be a team player and highly effective communicator capable of building strong cross-functional relationships.

jobs.description:
This is where
your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Summary

Baxter is committed to driving connectivity for patients, clinicians, and customers across healthcare settings. Baxter’s Connected Care Group
focuses on two critical areas: (1) Digital Products
, delivering connected devices and software to customers, and (2) Digital Platforms
, facilitating software development across Baxter’s medical devices with a unified architecture to accelerate customer-focused solutions. The portfolio includes key offerings that drive revenue and advance Baxter’s mission to save and sustain lives while shaping the future of healthcare.

The Director of Marketing, Connected Care Group serves as the marketing leader for Baxter's Connected Care portfolio, responsible for shaping portfolio growth strategy, customer adoption, market expansion, and commercial performance across Digital Products and Digital Platforms. In partnership with Product Management, Sales, and other cross-functional teams, this leader translates market opportunities, customer insights, and competitive dynamics into portfolio strategies that accelerate revenue growth, strengthen customer value realization, and expand market penetration.

This role owns portfolio positioning, marketing strategy, customer adoption strategy, and commercial growth initiatives while leading upstream and downstream marketing teams. The Director will modernize marketing capabilities through data-driven decision making, AI-enabled marketing approaches, customer adoption strategies, and scalable commercial processes that improve marketing effectiveness and business outcomes.

This role sits within the Connected Care Group and reports into the Senior Director of Product Management. There will be a team of 2-5 direct reports that will be responsible for driving growth of the portfolio. Key stakeholders in the Connected Care Group include Product Management, Sales, Marketing Communications (MarCom), Project Management, Operations, and R&D. Across the broader organization, she/he will also interact with other marketing, product management, medical affairs, sales, regional, and quality teams. She/he will have responsibility to communicate milestones and progress to BU leadership and executives as appropriate.

To be successful, this leader must balance near-term commercial priorities with long-term portfolio growth and market development objectives. The ideal candidate will be a strategic and data-driven marketing leader who can influence across a matrixed organization, build high-performing teams, and drive measurable business outcomes through modern marketing capabilities and customer-centric growth strategies.

This role requires adaptability in a fast-paced and evolving environment, balancing strategic leadership with operational engagement. Success requires a highly collaborative, visible leader who can effectively influence across virtual and in-person teams while navigating changing business priorities. While this is primarily a strategic leadership role, the Director is expected to remain close to execution and contribute directly where appropriate to ensure speed, quality, and alignment with business priorities. We are seeking a collaborative, high-energy, and agile individual who has an in-depth knowledge of the healthcare and technology ecosystem.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Core Responsibilities

Shape portfolio growth strategy and influence business unit priorities through market insights, customer understanding, competitive intelligence, and commercial analytics.
Lead upstream and downstream marketing teams to drive portfolio adoption, market expansion, customer value realization, and revenue growth across Connected Care offerings.
Build and modernize marketing capabilities, including customer adoption programs, digital and AI-enabled marketing approaches, commercial analytics, and scalable demand generation processes.
Ensure alignment between product strategy and commercial execution through effective positioning, go-to-market strategies, and cross-functional leadership.
Develop and lead a high-performing marketing organization while managing marketing investment to maximize business impact and ROI.

Marketing Capability and Commercial Transformation

Lead the modernization of marketing across Connected Care through data-driven decision making, AI-enabled marketing approaches, digital engagement strategies, and scalable commercial processes.
Establish metrics and analytics that connect marketing investments to customer adoption, pipeline creation, revenue growth, and marketing ROI.
Drive continuous improvement of marketing operations, customer journey management, demand generation, and portfolio performance measurement.

Upstream Marketing

Lead market and customer insight generation and partner with Product Management and business leadership to translate those insights into portfolio strategy, product investment priorities, market expansion opportunities, and long-term growth initiatives.
Own portfolio-level positioning and narrative, ensuring clear articulation of platform value and differentiation across interconnected solutions.
Analyze market size, growth, and competitive dynamics to inform strategic priorities; develop deep subject matter expertise across the portfolio.
Capture and communicate customer intelligence and other learnings back across the Baxter organization.
Understand key growth drivers and pricing.
Clarify the portfolio and product-specific value propositions and positioning relative to customer pain points and competitors.
Segment customers and inform priorities.
Understand decision-making and purchasing processes for customers.
Help craft internal and external messaging.
Develop OUS marketing plan and enable growth outside developed markets.
Create multi-year plans to build the Connected Care brand through a long- term marketing strategy.
Manage 1-3 Upstream Marketing individuals

Downstream Marketing

Ensure the organization has effective marketing processes, tools, content, and enablement capabilities required to support commercial success
Communicate and implement messaging across functional and geographic partners – and help shape their communications.
Develop and execute integrated marketing campaigns, content, and omnichannel strategies to drive awareness, demand generation, and sales enablement.
Develop segment-specific messaging, value propositions, and clinical/economic narratives to drive targeted campaigns and market engagement.
Deliver high-quality pre launch, launch, and post-launch promotional programs that maximize product adoption and penetration within the market.
Support regional commercial marketing teams to help achieve growth and profitability with support for messaging.
Work cross-functionally with business units, region/country teams, and functions to brainstorm, develop, launch new processes and improvements.
Work with internal teams to develop clinical and economic messaging.
Lead product launches, field sales support, and other marketing activities.
Generate/analyze competitive intelligence and promote understanding of competitive tactics with the sales team.
Partner with marketing communications to create innovative and forward-looking content to drive market awareness, lead generation, leading to deal closure.
Develop relationships and regularly interact with customers through presentations, interviews, tradeshows, professional societies, and site visits.
Collaborate with global portfolio marketing to understand issues related to product quality/customer complaints; ensure feedback is communicated back to respective owners for input into recommendations and resolution to identified issues.
Manage agencies and external stakeholders where needed.
Collaborate with Medical Affairs to aid in guiding high-value studies to support key claims in marketing materials and establish Baxter’s presence as a thought leader.
Manage 1-3 Downstream Marketing individuals.

Qualifications

Experience marketing complex, software-enabled or platform-based healthcare solutions, with a demonstrated ability to drive enterprise adoption.
Strong understanding of digital health ecosystems, including interoperability, clinical workflows, and enterprise IT environments.
Highly organized, self-starter who can lead and collaborate across the organization effectively.
Ability to operate with ambiguity in volatile environments, leading a function in and through the face of change, setting clear direction and guidance for the team you lead.
Ability to work and influence across business units and functions. Demonstrated track-record of leading and influencing in a matrixed environment.
Excellent written & verbal communication and presentation skills
Needs to work independently without supervision on most initiatives.
Team player with a strategic partnership mindset.
Must be available to travel to customer sites and team meetings frequently.
Entrepreneurial spirit and growth mindset.
Ability to prioritize and influence others while exercising proper judgement for sound decision making and trade-off analysis.
Strong ability to communicate effectively at all levels inside and outside of the organization.
Strong work ethic and comfort with ambiguity.
Experience and knowledge of trends shaping product development and customer behavior.
Take a collaborative approach by openly discussing issues in a way that brings out the best thinking, attitude, and performance in others. Works effectively and productively with others running functional and support areas. Consider effect of decisions on other parts of the company.
Ability to travel up to 50% of the time, including international.

Education And Experience

Requires a bachelor’s degree. MBA and/or graduate degree is a plus.
10+ years marketing experience (preferably in Healthcare IT) with a proven track record of developing and executing successful marketing campaigns.
10+ years of direct and cross-functional leadership
Technical understanding of IT and connected care environments and robust knowledge of clinical processes and workflows. Understanding of IP networking and enterprise IT/IoT solutions. Understanding of cloud and on-prem solutions.
Demonstrated career progression in previous roles.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Intern - Marketing - Copywriter
jobs.description:
Overview

Being good neighbors – helping people, investing in our communities, and making the world a better place – is who we are at State Farm. It is at the core of how we operate and the reason for our success. We're moving with urgency to become a Next Gen Good Neighbor, with technology that strengthens human connections and enhances the customer experience. As an employee, you'll spend less time navigating systems and more time applying judgment, empathy, and expertise in the moments that matter most.

Responsibilities

Grow Your Skills, Grow Your Potential

This intern will join a team within Enterprise Marketing focused on creating and improving digital content that helps customers find, understand and engage with State Farm online. The team brings together content strategy, copywriting, SEO, AI search and web expertise to improve experiences across statefarm.com and other digital channels.

This is an opportunity for an aspiring writer to gain hands-on experience creating content for a nationally recognized brand while learning how strong writing, customer needs, search behavior, brand standards and business goals come together. The intern will work alongside experienced writers, content strategists, SEO professionals and other marketing partners and will have opportunities to contribute to real consumer-facing work.

As an intern in this role, you will get to:

Write, edit and optimize consumer-facing digital content across formats such as articles, product and landing pages, FAQs, email, social content and video scripts.
Learn how copy changes based on the audience, channel, customer need and stage of the decision-making journey.
Use SEO and search insights to help create content that is useful, easy to find and aligned with what customers are looking for.
Research topics and translate complex insurance or financial concepts into clear, approachable language.
Partner with copywriters, content strategists, SEO professionals and other marketing teams to develop and improve content.
Participate in content reviews and learn how feedback, brand standards, accessibility, legal considerations and customer insights shape published work.
Explore responsible uses of generative AI for research, ideation, drafting and editing while applying human judgment to the final product.
Review content performance and learn how data and customer behavior can inform future writing and optimization.

Project work and training:

The intern is expected to complete one or more meaningful content projects during the summer, potentially including developing new digital content, optimizing existing content or helping create a connected set of content around a customer topic or need.

The intern will receive hands-on coaching and exposure to digital copywriting, editing, SEO and AI search fundamentals, content strategy, brand voice, accessibility and the processes required to publish consumer-facing content within a large organization. Project assignments may span multiple digital channels to help build a broader understanding of how copywriting works across the customer experience.

Qualifications

We are looking for:

Seeking a current Sophomore, Junior or Senior in an undergraduate program majoring in Communications, Journalism, English, Marketing, Public Relations, Advertising, or a related discipline, with a graduation date of December 2027 or later.
An ideal candidate will have experience with:
Strong writing, editing and proofreading skills, including familiarity with AP style.
Ability to write clearly and adapt content for different audiences, formats and purposes.
Experience collaborating across teams and incorporating different perspectives and feedback into solutions.
Ability to adapt across different types of work and priorities in a dynamic environment.
Strong attention to detail and willingness to receive and apply feedback.
Strong verbal, listening, and presentation skills.
Self-motivated and proactive with the ability to take ownership of assignments while seeking input and guidance when appropriate.

Preferred/Additional Experience

Interest in a career in copywriting, journalism, digital content, content marketing or a related field.
Coursework or experience in writing for digital channels, journalism, marketing, communications or advertising.
Writing samples or a portfolio demonstrating strong writing ability.
Familiarity with SEO, content management systems, analytics or digital marketing concepts.
Experience using generative AI tools responsibly for writing, research or ideation, with an understanding that AI-generated content requires review and editing.
Experience writing for multiple formats or audiences through coursework, student organizations, internships, freelance work, publications or personal projects.

Internship Program Eligibility:

To be eligible for the summer internship program, you must be a full-time student currently enrolled in an undergraduate or post-graduate program throughout the duration of the internship. Selected interns must reside within the continental U.S. for the duration of the summer internship.

Applicants are required to be eligible to lawfully work in the U.S. immediately; employer will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work authorization (e.g. H-1B visa) for this opportunity***

What You Can Expect:

The internship will occur between June 2, 2027 - August 11, 2027 (10 weeks)
Hours: Monday-Friday, 38.75 hours per week
Pay: $25/hour. In addition, interns selected for our summer internship program will be eligible for a $2,000 stipend (minus applicable taxes)!
Competitive candidates will be invited to participate in a pre-screening video
Due to the short duration of the summer program, it is an expectation that hired interns will be available for the duration of the summer internship with little to no disruption in work schedule.

Work Arrangement:

HYBRID: Selected interns should plan to spend time working from home and some time working in the office as part of our hybrid work environment. Please note that relocation benefits will not apply.

HOME/HUB LOCATIONs: Bloomington, IL

Next Steps!

Applicant volume and hiring needs may result in early closure or extension, so apply as soon as possible! To submit an application, click "Apply" on the job listing page on the State Farm career site.

Qualified and competitive candidates will be invited to participate in the interview process, with selected candidates progressing through two rounds of interviewing.

What’s In It For You:

Competitive pay and relaxed dress code

Direct experience you can leverage for your future career

An opportunity to learn and network with industry-leading influencers

Mentoring and Development to help you succeed

We love to give back! Being involved in volunteer opportunities to give back to the community.

We embrace Diversity and Inclusion: We are one team and it is simply the right thing to do!

We are not just offering an internship but the opportunity for a meaningful career! Come join our passionate team!

Our Benefits

We are excited to offer our interns a tailored set of benefits with a range of valuable perks to help support you during your time with us!

Time Off

40 hours of Life Leave
Military Leave

401(K) Savings Plan (Eligible at age 18)
Mutual Funds (Eligible at age 18)

Miscellaneous Benefits

jobs.title: Marketing Coordinator (contract)
jobs.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two Hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home and has since grown to over 4 million Hosts who have welcomed more than 1 billion guest arrivals in more than 100, 000 cities and towns located in 220+ countries and regions across the globe. Every day, Hosts offer unique stays and one-of-a-kind activities that make it possible for guests to experience the world in a more authentic, connected way.

Airbnb was born with a creative spirit, and it’s one of the most defining parts of our culture. We use our curiosity and imagination to come up with unconventional solutions. These are the ideas at the core of Airbnb:

Our community is based on connection and belonging.
Our creativity allows us to imagine new possibilities for people.
Our responsibility is to all of our stakeholders.
It takes a unified team committed to our core values to embody these ideas, and our fast-moving team is committed to leading as a 21st century company.

Job Overview:

The Marketing Coordinator will play a critical role in helping Airbnb.org deliver high-impact marketing programs. You’ll own the day-to-day coordination of our rapid response marketing during disasters, build the processes and tools that keep our marketing team running effectively, and support execution across brand, growth, and lifecycle marketing.

We are looking for a team player with a passion for marketing that wants to do good in the world. This role requires someone detail-oriented and organized that is a proactive problem-solver and expert communicator.

About Plug

Plug is the marketplace for used electric vehicles. Consumers get an instant cash offer backed by battery-health data, and dealers across the US bid in real time on that inventory. Former Tesla executives founded Plug in 2023. We’ve facilitated $150M in EV sales and raised a $20M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

Why Plug

You’ll own a piece of the biggest automotive infrastructure opportunity.
You’ll work on a platform built exclusively for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.
You’ll join an AI-native company. We’re rethinking how work gets done from the ground up.
You’ll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion-dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.
You’ll have real ownership, high autonomy, and a direct line to company outcomes.

The Role

Plug is hiring a Lifecycle Marketing Lead to shape how we communicate with customers at every stage of their relationship with Plug, from the moment they check their vehicle’s value through to close and beyond. Today, Sales, RevOps, BizOps, and Marketing split this work, with no single owner. This role is critical to the business’s growth.

This is a senior, hands-on role. You’ll set strategy, write copy, and run execution from day one, with real technical depth in marketing automation. This isn't a production role that receives prewritten briefs. You’ll take an open problem from idea to measured result. You’re welcome to bring in support when it serves the work, and you can build and lead a team as the function grows.

What You’ll Do

Work with Product, BizOps, and Sales to understand the core issues across the funnel.
Lead lifecycle strategy, copy, and execution for customer-facing email and SMS, replacing the current ad hoc process spread across multiple teams.
Set up behavior-triggered flows to replace one-off sends decided manually.
Work with RevOps on the technical build. How much you build directly versus specify is flexible. Setting up triggers is part of the role.
Create the content plan and editorial calendar for customers, building trust and value over time.
Turn content into nurture journeys and track how well they move customers through their lifecycle.
Email and SMS are the first priority. Retargeting and on-site personalization (pop-ups, banners, personalized homepage content) are nice-to-have.

What Success Looks Like In The First Six Months

Set a clear operating rhythm for lifecycle campaigns.
Own a meaningful set of campaigns from strategy through results.
Launch a stronger nurture or onboarding journey with a defined test-and-measure plan.
Implement consistent briefs, segmentation rules, QA checks, and post-campaign reviews.

What You’ll Bring

6+ years in lifecycle or retention marketing, with experience setting strategy and running campaigns independently
Hands-on experience with marketing automation platforms
Strong copywriting skills, with comfort writing and refining messaging from start to finish
Experience designing behavior-triggered, segmented campaigns
Experience working across functions with Sales and RevOps

Not sure you should apply? We’d still like to hear from you. If you don’t meet every item in What You’ll Bring but you’re excited about this work, just apply.

Performance Metrics

Funnel completion rate, measured by the reduction in drop-off between key moments in the customer journey
Reactivation rate and time to conversion for nurtured leads who return within the three- to six-month window
Email and SMS engagement health (open rate, click-through rate, list growth, and unsubscribe rate)
Conversion influenced by lifecycle touchpoints

Annual salary: $145,000 to $180,000

jobs.title: Sr Product Marketing Mgr, Go-To-Market
jobs.description:
ABOUT OBLQ

OBLQ builds software for independent insurance agencies, providing technology solutions that help independent P&Cs operate more efficiently and grow faster. We handle the technology so agencies can focus on selling policies and driving revenue. Learn more at oblq.ai.

Same Team. More Agency.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager to help turn our products that deliver for existing customers into a company and category that independent insurance agencies know about, understand, and want to buy.

You'll work directly with the founders and stay close to both the product and our customers. You'll learn how independent agencies operate, what slows their teams down, why they buy, what makes them skeptical, and how OBLQ changes the economics of their business. Then you'll turn those insights into the way we go to market.

You'll own product positioning, messaging, launches, customer stories, sales enablement, competitive intelligence, and much of the content that connects OBLQ to the market.

This is an early-stage role. We have products our customers love, we have great data and measurable results, a brand, and a point of view. We need someone who can take those raw materials and build a repeatable product marketing engine around them.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Position OBLQ and its products.
Develop clear positioning and messaging for OBLQs current and future products. Understand what matters to agency owners & agents, and translate complex product capabilities into simple reasons to care.

Own the product story.
Make sure our website, social presence, sales materials, demos, campaigns, and product launches tell a consistent and compelling story.

Know the customer.
Spend time with independent agency owners and agents. Understand how they generate leads, quote business, work with carriers, use their CRM, follow up with customers, and make technology decisions.

Turn customer outcomes into proof.
Build case studies, customer stories, ROI narratives, testimonials, and other evidence that helps prospective customers understand what OBLQ can do for their agency.

Build sales enablement.
Give the people selling OBLQ what they need to have better conversations: messaging, presentations, one-pagers, competitive positioning, objection handling, demo narratives, follow-up materials, and customer-specific stories.

Own product launches.
Create the go-to-market plan for new capabilities, carrier integrations, product releases, and future OBLQ products. Define the audience, message, channels, assets, and measures of success.

Understand the market.
Know the insurance technology landscape, the alternatives agencies use today, and where OBLQ fits. Track competitors, comparative raters, agency management systems, CRMs, automation products, and emerging technologies that could change the market.

Build content that earns attention.
Create and manage content for the channels where our customers spend time. That may include LinkedIn, customer email, website content, product education, thought leadership, webinars, industry communities, and other formats we discover work.

Improve how we generate demand.
Work across organic, outbound, partnerships, referrals, and paid acquisition to understand which messages and channels create qualified interest. Test quickly, measure results, and keep what works.

Bring the market back into the product.
You won't own the product roadmap, but you'll have an important voice in it. Bring customer feedback, competitive intelligence, win/loss insights, and market signals back into product decisions.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You have experience marketing B2B software products and can show examples where your work changed how a product was understood, sold, adopted, or launched.

You know how to find the useful insight inside a customer conversation and turn it into positioning or messaging people actually understand.

You can explain a complicated product simply without stripping away what makes it valuable.

You understand the difference between describing a feature and explaining why someone should care about it.

You're comfortable creating the strategy and doing the work. At this stage, you may define the launch plan in the morning and write the landing page in the afternoon.

You can work closely with product and engineering teams and become technically fluent enough to market what we're building accurately.

You use data to evaluate your work. You care about pipeline, conversion, engagement, adoption, and revenue more than impressions for their own sake.

You're comfortable operating with incomplete information and creating structure where it doesn't yet exist.

You have strong judgment about brand and messaging. You know when something needs another round of thinking and when it just needs to get into the market so we can learn.

SKILLS WE'RE INTERESTED IN

Working with AI tools to accelerate research, content, experimentation, and execution
B2B SaaS or vertical SaaS
Insurance or insurtech (nice to have)
Products sold to small and midsize businesses
Workflow automation or operational software
Product-led or founder-led companies moving toward a repeatable GTM model
Sales enablement and customer storytelling
Launching new or unfamiliar product categories
Competitive and market research
Demand generation and lifecycle marketing

Insurance experience is not a prerequisite. We care more about your ability to understand a market quickly and turn what you learn into effective product marketing.

HOW WE WORK

Our development cycle is fast. New capabilities can move from idea to working software quickly, which means product marketing needs to stay equally close to the product and the customer.

We value people who understand the problem, form a point of view, communicate it clearly, put it into the market, measure what happens, and improve it.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

A year from now:
An independent agency owner can land on OBLQ and quickly understand what we do, why it's different, and why it matters to their business.
Our positioning and messaging are consistent everywhere a prospect encounters us.
Customer outcomes have become credible stories, proof points, and sales assets.
Product launches have an audience, message, plan, and measurement strategy before they ship.
Sales conversations are supported by strong materials and a clear understanding of customer objections and competitive alternatives.
We know which messages, audiences, and channels create qualified opportunities and we're investing more heavily in the ones that work.
What we're learning in the market is consistently making its way back into the product.
Our product marketing capability is repeatable and can scale with the company.

Product & Packaging initiatives that build consumer trust, transparency, brand credibility, and stakeholder alignment.
